THE CALL (structured, auditable — no threshold, no lookup table, no formula anywhere in this decision):
- `vehicle` — any menu instrument from `state.park_menu` (KEEP = today's `state.park_policy_current.vehicle`)
- `conviction` — HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW + a numeric `conviction_pct`
- `rationale` — one paragraph explicitly addressing why this instrument beats the runner-up
- `invalidation` — the observable development that would flip this call. **SYMMETRIC EVIDENTIARY STANDARD (2026-08-18).** State it at the same bar as the evidence that justified the CURRENT position, in both directions. Concretely: if a de-risk out of the default vehicle was made on a narrative/judgment case, the conditions for returning must not be a conjunctive numeric checklist — and vice versa. This is a discipline about how the criteria are WRITTEN, not a threshold or a rule table; the call itself remains AI judgment end to end (`PARK_ROUTER_DESIGN.md` §1), and naming criteria never binds a later session against its own judgment. **Why it matters structurally, not for performance:** the 2026-07-26 directive retired every anti-churn rail and named *next-session reversibility* as the compensating control for having none. A re-entry bar materially harder to clear than the exit bar makes the defensive position sticky and quietly removes that control. Worked precedent: the 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-02 KEEP-SGOV calls named a conjunctive re-entry bar ("30Y sustained below ~5.10% AND September hike odds under ~50% AND a confirmed Hormuz reopening — any one alone is not enough") after an exit justified narratively; the 30Y was still 5.31% on 2026-08-17, so honoring that bar literally would have held the park in SGOV through VOO 684.56 → 706.23 (~$265 of foregone return on the park as then sized). The 2026-08-03 SWITCH correctly overrode it — the self-correction worked, and this note exists so the next session does not have to rely on catching it.
- `theater_check` — a one-line self-audit that the rationale isn't narrating a foregone conclusion

Default-KEEP on ambiguity — the same high-bar, default-NO posture as the ANALYSIS — REGIME CHECK flag above. `Daily.md` gets a mandatory `## PARK ALLOCATION CALL` section carrying the five fields above, every trading day, including a KEEP day.

**GRADED ALLOCATION — THE CALL NOW CARRIES A TARGET FRACTION (activated on live capital 2026-09-04,
owner directive; `PARK_ALLOCATOR_V4_DESIGN.md` §2.3, `bigquery/216`/`218`/`220`/`221`).** The park is a
TWO-SLEEVE book: a risk sleeve (default VOO) and a defensive sleeve (default SGOV), with a defensive
fraction **f in {0, 25, 50, 75, 100}**. The call emits `target_f_pct` alongside the sleeves; a "switch"
is a WEIGHT DELTA, not a vehicle swap, and f=0 / f=100 remain legal and mean exactly what VOO-only and
SGOV-only always meant.

  - **Read `state.park_axis_daily` for today.** It publishes, mechanically, each axis's LEVEL
    (defensive or not, from its last MEASURED reading) and EVENT (`is_firing` = ENTERED defensive
    within 2 sessions), plus `standing_defensive_count`, `firing_count`, `cap_pct`,
    `increase_gate_open` and `testable_axes`. **A standing state is never news** — that distinction is
    the whole point, and is the defect behind the 2026-09-01 record counting a three-week-old
    `shock_overlay='acute'` as same-session deterioration.
  - **MIXED VINTAGE — CHECK `measured_on` PER AXIS.** On a live D1 run the four price-derived axes
    (volatility, credit, index, shock) are **ALWAYS one session behind**: D1 runs 16:12-16:36 MT and
    D2a, whose STEP 1d writes `events.signal_marks`, does not start until 16:41 MT. Only `breadth` is
    same-session, and only because D1 wrote `EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT` itself minutes earlier. This is
    structural, not an outage — `axes_measured_today` on the same view counts the fresh ones. Where
    your own live readings contradict a carried axis, record it in `fields.axis_overrides` with the
    reading and its as-of date. **The mechanical count may NOT BLOCK or DEMOTE a de-risk on an axis
    whose `measured_on` is not today** — that would let yesterday's stale quiet veto today's observed
    deterioration. The ratchet still holds the other way: a carried axis may never be counted as
    FIRING, because an event is by definition a change and a carried reading is not evidence of one.
  - **CAP — `park_axis_daily.cap_pct` IS THE RAW CAP, NOT THE ONE YOU CLAMP TO.** It is
    `LEAST(100, 25 x standing_defensive_count)` off TODAY's standing count alone. The cap f is actually
    clamped to is the DECAY-CONFIRMED cap of the next bullet, which is STICKY — it holds high while a
    lower standing count is still being confirmed. These are different numbers: measured 2026-09-04
    they disagree on **8 of 68** live sessions, maximum gap **75pp** (2026-06-05: raw 25, confirmed
    100). The confirmed cap is PATH-DEPENDENT and is **not** recoverable from any fixed-width window
    over `cap_pct` — a 3-session `MAX`, the obvious approximation, misses all eight. Compute the clamp
    in-session per the DECAY bullet; `analytics.park_ladder_shadow.confirmed_cap_pct` is the same
    quantity computed retrospectively, for reconciliation only. Note the confirmed cap is >= the raw
    cap on every session measured, so it is a CEILING that the one-way ratchet below forbids you from
    using to license a larger de-risk than your own hand-scoring supports.
  - **INCREASING f (de-risking) requires the gate:** at least one axis ENTERED defensive within 2
    sessions AND `standing_defensive_count >= 2`. A single standing axis never engages an increase —
    that is the landed cardinality floor, preserved, and all 15 measured one-day single-axis episodes
    in history cost $0.
  - **CONVICTION SIZES IT.** Suggested target = the step NEAREST to `conviction_pct x cap_pct`, ties
    round DOWN, never above cap. You may deviate by ±1 step with a NAMED reason. Worked: MEDIUM-60 at
    cap 50 -> 30 -> **25**. HIGH-95 at cap 100 -> 95 -> **100**. Conviction-85 at cap 100 -> **75**.
    This is the owner's specific ask made mechanical: a MEDIUM-60 two-axis de-risk no longer moves the
    same capital as a HIGH-95 four-axis one.
  - **DECAY IS AUTOMATIC AND YOU MUST STATE IT.** Each session f is clamped to the confirmed cap. The
    cap steps DOWN only on the first session at which the lower standing count has ALREADY held on the
    two preceding measured sessions (three consecutive readings, step on the third); a clamp from
    f >= 50 unwinds at most ONE step per session; a clamp crossing only 25->0 executes immediately; and
    a crisis-entered increase is exempt from the clamp for 2 sessions. **Compute the clamped f, state
    the arithmetic in the rationale, and emit the clamped value** — decay never happens outside a
    session, which is precisely what keeps this AI judgment inside rails rather than a rule table
    running the book (`PARK_ROUTER_DESIGN.md` §1's rejection of v1 turns on exactly that distinction).
  - **DECREASING f is always allowed and never delayed** — re-risks have measured RIGHT (both the
    2026-08-03 and 2026-09-03 re-entries were correct).
  - **CRISIS OVERRIDE:** a single-session index move <= -2.5% or VIX >= 28 lifts the cap to 100 that
    session.
  - **Log `target_f_pct`, `risk_sleeve`, `defensive_sleeve` in `fields`** alongside the existing keys.
    `vehicle` stays populated as the MAJORITY sleeve (tie at f=50 -> the risk sleeve), because
    `dbt/models/sources.yml` carries a live `not_null` test on it.

**FORWARD TEST IS RUNNING — this is not a settled system.** Activated 2026-09-04 against a measured
record that does NOT flatter it: over 15 historical episodes the defensive signal had mean forward edge
−0.638pp (SD 1.308) and won only 4 of 15, and across the three shadow episodes the ladder beat the
binary path every time (**+2.30 / +2.72 / +0.84pp** against the explicit binary counterfactual arm; CORRECTED 2026-09-04 from +1.62 / +1.56 / +0.84, which was measured before two defects were fixed — the STRICT decay was implemented as a trailing MAX rather than three-consecutive-readings, and the binary comparison was inferred from the policy vehicle STRING instead of scored as its own arm) while trailing never-switching every time (−1.09 /
−0.91 / −0.63pp). Read that as: GRADING beats the all-or-nothing switch, and de-risking at all still
costs against simply holding VOO. W5's PARK FORWARD-TEST COUNTDOWN forces the re-evaluation after
three post-activation episodes.

**DE-RISK EVIDENCE CARDINALITY (added 2026-09-03; SUPERSEDED as the SIZING rule by the graded ladder
above, RETAINED as its floor — a single standing axis still licenses no increase).** A **de-risk** — a SWITCH to a LOWER `state.park_menu.risk_tier` than today's opening `state.park_policy_current.vehicle` — converts the park only when **at least two INDEPENDENT evidence axes fire in the same session**. The axes are: **volatility** (VIX in any form), **breadth**, **index level/trend** (the index against its moving averages or its trailing closing high), **rates** (the 10Y, policy-path odds, the curve), **credit** (`hy_oas`, HY/IG spreads), and **shock/commodity** (`shock_overlay`, Brent, a named geopolitical channel). **Two readings on the SAME axis are ONE axis** — VIX below 15 outright and VIX below its own 20d is one axis, not two; that is the whole point of the rule. If exactly one axis fires, D1 calls **KEEP** and records `fields.park_watch = true` plus `fields.watch_axis` naming the axis that fired and what a second, independent axis would have to do to carry a de-risk; the call is then re-decided **fresh next session on next session's evidence**, exactly like any other KEEP. This is **not** a cooldown, a budget, a conviction gate, or an approval step — nothing is deferred to another party, no later session is bound by it, and a two-axis de-risk still binds and converts the SAME DAY at ANY conviction, precisely as before. **Re-risks and laterals are NOT subject to this rule** and are unchanged in every respect. D2 needs no change: a WATCH is an ordinary bound KEEP, and D2 already no-ops when the called vehicle equals the current policy vehicle.

**Why — measured 2026-09-03 (interactive-session probe), not inferred.** The 2026-09-01 de-risk fired on **ONE** axis (breadth); VIX's own clause explicitly did NOT fire, Brent missed by $0.35 and the VIX-50d leg by 0.11. The 2026-09-03 re-entry required **TWO** axes and got them on both limbs each. Exit on one, return on two — cheap to leave and dear to return, which is backwards for a park whose default vehicle is the risk asset. The 2026-08-18 SYMMETRIC EVIDENTIARY STANDARD above **cannot see this**: it compares clause KIND and HEIGHT, never clause **CARDINALITY**, so the two rules are complements and neither replaces the other. Measured cost of that one round trip: **$214.32** to the 2026-09-03 close (foregone VOO appreciation $215.61 against $3.03 SGOV carry and $1.75 commissions; execution was clean, slippage was $12.88 FAVORABLE), plus a wash-sale disallowance originally recorded as **$107.73 of the $149.18 realized loss** and twice corrected since. **(i)** SUPERSEDED 2026-09-04 by `bigquery/219`: the pre-rebuy figure is **$0.00**, because 13 of its 14 "replacements" were the sale's own basis seen through sibling legs of the same exchange-split order — a full liquidation was being washed by itself. **(ii)** The "of the $149.18" framing MIXES TWO BASES and they must never be netted: IBKR reports **−$149.18** account-level on AVERAGE-COST basis, while the repo's FIFO lot ledger (`analytics.park_tax_lots`, 20 fragments, 21.888 sh) reports **−$100.06** for the same liquidation — of which the losing legs are −$107.73 and the winning legs +$7.67. The **$49.12** gap is a BASIS-METHOD SEAM, not an un-disallowed remainder, and an earlier version of this sentence read it as one. The realized loss itself is broker-tied and unaffected throughout, and the 09-04 rebuy — FILLED at the broker 2026-09-04 13:30 UTC (VOO 21 @ 709.89 ARCA + 0.4714 @ 709.83 IBKR = the staged 21.4714), with the repo figure flipping when that session's D2a records it into events.parking_events — IS a genuine replacement and disallows essentially the whole $107.73 (`state.wash_sale_exposure`). Segment-scored on `analytics.park_counterfactuals` (AI era, anchor 2026-07-24), **both defensive excursions this allocator has taken have lost ground** (0-for-2): −2.841pp (SGOV 07-27..08-04) and −1.019pp (SGOV 09-02..09-03) — the two CLOSED defensive excursions of the AI era; the intervening −0.352pp (VOO 08-04..09-02) is the RISK-ON segment between them and is NOT a defensive excursion; AI +1.073% against never-switching VOO +4.650%. Note the reversal itself was NOT a freak: conditional on that exit state the re-entry set cleared within two sessions in 33.3% of 42 historical analogues, so the timing was genuinely unlucky — what was not luck is that a single-axis MEDIUM-60 de-risk was permitted to move ~97% of NAV at all.

**Counterfactual check — the test any rail here must pass, and DO NOT re-propose the alternatives.** This rule sends 2026-09-01 to WATCH, and leaves BOTH re-risks untouched: 2026-08-03 (a re-risk) and 2026-09-03 (a re-risk, and two axes regardless). It also leaves PA-01's three-axis crisis de-risk binding same-day. The **retired** rails do the opposite and were re-measured this session: a **5-day cooldown** blocks only the RE-ENTRY, holding the park in SGOV through ~09-08 while VOO rallied — a DEEPER loss, not a shorter one — and a **HIGH-conviction re-risk gate** blocks BOTH re-risks the allocator has ever made (08-03 and 09-03 were each MEDIUM 60), which would have stranded the park in SGOV from 07-26 through VOO ~690 → ~710. Both are strictly worse than doing nothing; do not re-propose either. The allocator already applied this discipline informally — clauses fired on 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-31 and it declined to flip both times.

**IMMEDIATE BINDING (owner directive 2026-07-26 — loop `park_allocator` is `active_auto` in `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml`; Operating_Protocols.md §13.F; qualified for de-risks ONLY by the DE-RISK EVIDENCE CARDINALITY rule directly above, 2026-09-03).** Every well-formed call logs `status='BOUND'` the same day — a SWITCH (de-risk, lateral, or re-risk) at ANY conviction, or a KEEP (trivially BOUND, since D2's PARK ALLOCATION CONVERSION step already no-ops when the called vehicle equals the current policy vehicle — the "bound KEEP" case below). No conviction gate, no budget/cooldown check, and no next-session concurrence check gates whether `'BOUND'` is assigned. The only other status is `'HOLD'`, reserved for the connectors-down / evidence-ungatherable case below — D2 acts on any `status='BOUND'` call.

**LOGGED EVERY DAY, INCLUDING KEEP DAYS** (the daily no-change record is what makes calibration and the Q1 retrospective possible): `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(..., entry_type='park-allocation', ...)` with `fields` JSON carrying `{vehicle, conviction, conviction_pct, direction, status, readings}` (`status` is `'BOUND'` or `'HOLD'` only, per IMMEDIATE BINDING above) — `direction` = de-risk / lateral / re-risk / keep relative to today's opening `state.park_policy_current.vehicle`; `readings` = the evidence snapshot gathered above (VIX, hy_oas, the FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS values, `park_signal_daily` context). This is what `state.park_allocation_latest` surfaces to D2.

**READINGS PROVENANCE — EVERY CITED NUMBER MUST BE IN `fields.readings` (added 2026-09-04, park v4 Phase 1 evidence integrity; `PARK_ALLOCATOR_V4_DESIGN.md` §2.5).** Any numeric claim the rationale makes — an index level, a VIX print, a breadth reading, a sector count, a consecutive-session count — must appear in `fields.readings` as a key carrying the VALUE, its SOURCE, and its AS-OF date. A number that appears only in prose is not evidence; it is an assertion, and this system has now measured that assertion class failing twice in two consecutive sessions: `bigquery/213` corrected the 2026-09-01 record's "eight of eleven GICS sectors lower" (measured seven, and the four that rose were the three defensives plus energy, making the corrected pattern defensive rotation rather than the indiscriminate repricing the figure was recruited to prove — LOAD-BEARING, it was the stated ground for expiring the prior session's override), and `bigquery/214` corrected the 2026-09-03 record's "third consecutive improving session" (measured the second; harmless, because the clause it cleared asked for two). **COUNTS ARE COMPUTED, NEVER ASSERTED:** a consecutive-session count, a how-many-of-N count, or a threshold-crossing count must be derived from a series the readings name — `state.park_axis_daily` computes the axis-level and event-level counts mechanically and is the reference for anything it covers.

**AXIS SCORING IS ADVISORY, AND THE RATCHET IS ONE-WAY.** `state.park_axis_daily` (`bigquery/216`) publishes a mechanical LEVEL and EVENT per axis. D1 may consult it and MUST record any disagreement in `fields.axis_overrides` with a named reason. The AI's own hand-scoring remains authoritative for ACTION — this **survived the 2026-09-04 Phase-3 activation and is not scoped to any phase**; activation made the ladder SIZE the call, it did not make the mechanical count authoritative over the session's own reading — and the mechanical count may only BLOCK or DEMOTE a conversion whose rationale overstates its evidence — it may NEVER upgrade a KEEP into a conversion, nor a one-axis call into a two-axis one. That direction is deliberate and measured: mechanical scoring finds MORE two-axis days than the AI hand-counted, and unratcheted it would have turned the landed cardinality rule's correct $0 KEEP on 2026-09-01 into a full conversion.

**HEARTBEAT (every D1 firing, regardless of outcome — the `meta_monitoring_heartbeat` dead-man's-switch marker, `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml`):** `INSERT INTO ops.heartbeat (source, note) VALUES ('loop:park_allocator', '<vehicle> call, status=<status>')`.

**CONNECTORS-DOWN / EVIDENCE UNGATHERABLE:** no call binds — log `status='HOLD'` and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','D1','park_router', 'evidence ungatherable — park allocation HOLD', '<JSON>')` (`park_router` category, auto-resolvable next clean run).
