```
## W4. Weekly Research Handoff — regular routine

Runs after W1, W2, W3 are all saved. Converts distinct weekly research into idempotent queue work; D2 remains the sole daily revalidation and order-conversion owner.

```
Read access scope: Weekly cadence. Query `events.decision_log` (+ `analytics.find_precedents()`) bounded to the recent operationally-relevant window — all history, queryable, no live/archive split (§15). Read `Strategy.md`, `Experiment_Parameters.md`, `Operating_Protocols.md`, `Watchlist.md`, `B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md` as relevant (positions from `state.current_positions`, regime from `state.current_regime`, decisions from `events.decision_log`).

**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (generalized guard; W4 is catchup-safe).** FIRST, before the dependency gate or any read/write: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='W4' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "W4 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or W4's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY. Also END if another session's `'started'` W4 row for today exists with `log_ts` within the last 3 hours and no terminal row. W4's idempotent queue-only handoff is safe to catch up, but never to duplicate.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('W4', ['W1', 'W2', 'W3'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log, before anything else in this routine.** Aborts (RAISE) + raises a `missing_dependency` critical if W1, W2, or W3 have no `completed` run anywhere in the current weekly period — W1/W2/W3/W4 are `weekly_sun`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any W1/W2/W3 completion with `run_date BETWEEN` that week's Sunday `AND` today, not only a completion on this exact calendar day (this is also what fixed the pre-existing false-positive on a W4 running Monday afternoon against a Sunday-completed W1/W2/W3); self-bootstrapping. This is the general rule from Observability § above, restated here because it is the one call in this routine that must never be skipped (a 2026-07-09 audit found an analogous D2 session skip this exact call for its own dependency, so it is now inlined per-routine rather than left to a shared preamble alone).

**NO W4 STAGING GATE EXISTS.** W4 no longer detects mechanical exits or crafts any order, so it must not read/raise the trading-enable gate, invoke broker tools, call an order guard, write staged-order or position-lifecycle records, or create a calendar confirmation. It may always write idempotent `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entries and Watchlist changes. D2 performs the only revalidation and capital-movement decision under its own daily gates.

Read the just-saved weekly research files:
- `Weekly_Catalyst_Calendar.md` (W1 — Strategy A and C shortlists)
- `Weekly_Post_Event_Screen.md` (W2 — Strategy B shortlist)
- `Weekly_Position_Deep_Dive.md` (W3 — per-position hold/weekly-thesis-action/research recommendations + weekly-only action flag)

**BOUNDARY: no direct exit or order staging.** Do not repeat D1's mechanical detection (convergence, time exit, option-expiry mechanics, or daily development-triggered invalidation); do not call broker order tools, order guards, `state.open_orders`, `events.position_events`, or Calendar MCP. D2 is the only routine that revalidates and converts either daily or weekly action findings. W4's only conversion is an idempotent `PENDING_ANALYSIS` handoff plus its distinct W1/W2 research queues and Watchlist work.

A. WEEKLY-ONLY THESIS ACTIONS FROM W3 — for each `weekly-thesis-action` recommendation or `WEEKLY-THESIS-ACTION` flag, insert one due-today `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry for D2 with the exact cumulative criterion, W3 evidence span, D1 windows already reviewed, and conservative default. Idempotently check open and terminal queue history plus relevant `events.decision_log` first; use a stable item key `weekly-thesis-<strategy>-<ticker>-<W3 ISO week>-<criterion-key>`. This handoff asks D2 to independently revalidate and, only if still confirmed, perform the sole order conversion. It is never an exit instruction and carries no staged-order write.

(Thesis construction and research deferrals are no longer scheduled as human-pasted calendar events. W4 enqueues them to the `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue (`events.queue_events`); the daily D2 routine drains and runs them in-session, each as an isolated sub-task for fresh context. This keeps W4 light at high fan-out and incurs at most ~1 day latency — negligible against B's 10-day window.)

B. RESEARCH DEFERRALS FROM W3 — for each position with recommendation "further research":
   - Enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`): analysis_type research-deferral-checkpoint; the position's ticker/strategy; due_date = the date the resolving information becomes available (next trading day if already available); context = the specific information gap from W3 + reference to Strategy.md exit rules + "D2 must resolve the gap under its daily conversion rules"; conservative_default = exit the position if unresolved on due_date.

C. THESIS CONSTRUCTION FROM W2 (Strategy B) — for the W2 top-tier shortlist:
   - **ROUTER GATE FIRST — check `state.current_regime` (scope `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, key `B`) before enqueuing anything (limb added 2026-08-23 by W4; this codifies three consecutive cycles of actual behaviour and closes a spec gap referred to W5 on 2026-08-09 and again on 2026-08-17 that was never actioned).** If B is **DO-NOT-ACTIVATE**, the router bars every NEW B entry (`Strategy.md`'s Regime router section — the DO-NOT-ACTIVATE definition: no new entries, existing positions run to normal exits), so a thesis-construction row could only ever resolve to a foregone decline: enqueue **no** B thesis, route the top-tier candidates to the `Watchlist.md` "Strategy B watch overflow" section instead, marked **router-gated, not rank-gated**, and record the disposition. If B is **ACTIVATE**, proceed with the bullets below unchanged. This is the exact structure §D already carries for Strategy A ("If DO-NOT-ACTIVATE → route to Watchlist.md A-queue … no thesis"), and it is a **strategy gate, not a load cap** — the "no per-week cap, no overflow to Watchlist.md" wording below governs CAPACITY only and never licenses enqueuing into a closed router. Cycles 2026-W32, 2026-W34 (Mon) and 2026-W34 (Sun) each reached this outcome by inference, and W2's own file directs it in advance ("W4 must not enqueue these as staged entries while the DNA stands"). **Known and accepted cost, do not re-litigate it here:** a B window is only 10 trading days, so a router-gated candidate expires ungraded rather than waiting for a flip. That is the router doing its job; the calibration question about the router/window interaction belongs to W5 and M1a, not to W4.
   - Enqueue one `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`) per top-tier candidate (no per-week cap, no overflow to Watchlist.md): analysis_type thesis-construction; strategy B; due_date per the **HARD CHECK** below; context = B-specific enrichment from W2 + the originating D1 research-screen decision id + Strategy.md B criteria + B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md + Operating_Protocols.md; conservative_default = decline (no entry) if the entry window closes unresolved. **Deterministic event-identity dedupe is mandatory:** before INSERT, inspect both open and terminal queue history plus relevant `events.decision_log` for `analysis_type='thesis-construction'`, strategy B, ticker, and `qualifying_event_date`. **KEY-FORMAT PIN (corrected 2026-08-23 by W4, on a defect W2 2026-W34 found and assigned to W4 as the owner of the enqueue-key format; W4 independently confirmed it against the table the same day).** Use exactly `item_key = thesis-<TICKER>-B-<YYYYMMDD>` — e.g. `thesis-MSCI-B-20260726`. **This is a correction of the specification to match production, not a change to production.** Every one of the ~40 B thesis rows ever written to `events.queue_events` uses this shape (`thesis-CARR-B-20260803`, `thesis-ISRG-B-20260719`, …); the shape this document previously mandated — `thesis-B-<ticker>-<qualifying_event_date>` — has **never been written by any routine**, and `SELECT … WHERE item_key LIKE 'thesis-B-%'` returns **zero rows** against the whole table. A session performing the documented dedupe as a literal string match would therefore have found "no prior identity" *always*, including for an event already enqueued — a false-negative that duplicates a thesis and, downstream, a position. Writing the old shape now would have been worse than the status quo: it would have split the identity space into two incompatible key families and orphaned all existing history from any key-based check. **So: match on the FIELDS `(item_type='thesis-construction', strategy='B', ticker, due_date)`, never on the key string** — that field-based match is what makes the dedupe correct regardless of key shape, and it is what the 2026-08-23 W2 and W4 runs both actually used. Skip only that already represented event, never every event for a ticker; a later distinct event remains eligible. Carry `qualifying_event_date` and all originating D1/W2 decision ids in the payload. Order by days-remaining-in-window (fewer first) so D2 prioritizes.
   - **HARD CHECK — due_date MUST be the earliest-doable date, NEVER a next-trading-day default (earliest-wins; §"In-session analysis and the Pending_Analysis.md queue").** W2 only shortlists names whose qualifying move has ALREADY REALIZED (the Operating_Protocols.md §19 significance judgment operates on realized closes, and PART 2 additionally requires B's frozen ≥5% event-day spec floor — either way the Day-0 close is by definition already in for every W2 candidate) → **due_date = today** (the W4 run date, America/Denver from `state.trading_day_today.today`), **even when today is a weekend/holiday** (analysis needs no live market; only the resulting order-confirmation event must land on a trading session). The ONLY legitimate future due_date in this section is the §E deconfliction case (1 trading day after an expected exit fill). Do NOT push due_date to "the next trading day", "the next D2 run", or "the Monday open" for cadence/load convenience — that is the forbidden "pushed later for load" pattern, and it needlessly force-declines near-expiry candidates whose entry window closes within a day or two (the 2026-06-21 W4 run mis-stamped all 8 B-theses to the next session, which would have auto-declined WIX whose window closed 6/22 had D2 not re-dated them). **Self-verify before the INSERTs (earliest-wins, not "always today"):** a future (after-today) due_date is legitimate ONLY when (a) §E deconfliction applies, or (b) the candidate's qualifying Day-0 close genuinely has not printed yet — in which case set due_date to the date that close lands (the earliest the analysis can actually run). Case (b) cannot occur for a W2 shortlist (every rankable W2 candidate's qualifying move, hence its Day-0 close, is by definition already in — §19 judges realized moves only), so in practice every §C row is due today. What is forbidden is pushing due_date later for cadence/load convenience (next-trading-day / next-D2 / Monday-open defaulting); if a row would post a later due_date for any reason other than (a) or (b), correct it to the earliest-doable date before writing.

D. THESIS CONSTRUCTION FROM W1 (Strategy A and C) — for the W1 top-tier shortlists:
   - **DIRECTION FILTER FIRST — drop `DIRECTION-INADMISSIBLE` names before anything else in this limb (added 2026-09-06, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE; the W4 half of W1 PART 2's DIRECTION ADMISSIBILITY rail — read that entry for the measurement).** Strategy A is long-only, so a W1 candidate whose hypothesized mispricing is that the name is OVER-valued cannot produce an A entry and must not consume a thesis slot or an A-queue row. Discard any top-10 name carrying W1's `DIRECTION-INADMISSIBLE (A long-only rail)` mark — **and check direction yourself from the candidate's own field (a) rather than trusting the mark's presence**, since a pre-2026-09-06 `Weekly_Catalyst_Calendar.md` predates the rail and carries no marks at all (the 2026-08-30 shortlist ranked a bearish AMAT at #3). **Backfill the slot from the next admissible candidate** so the limb still converts a full top-10 rather than shipping a short one, and name the dropped candidates in this run's `<note>`.
   - Strategy A top-tier (top-10, after the direction filter above): check `state.current_regime` / most-recent M1 A router. If DO-NOT-ACTIVATE → route to Watchlist.md A-queue (reason "router gate; queued for next M1 ACTIVATE"); no thesis. If ACTIVATE → enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`) per top-tier name (analysis_type thesis-construction; strategy A; due_date today; context from W1 + Strategy.md/Operating_Protocols.md refs; conservative_default decline), ordered by catalyst-date proximity. No per-week cap. (The DO-NOT-ACTIVATE gate is a strategy gate, not a load cap.)
   - Strategy C top-tier (top-5): enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`) per top-tier name (analysis_type thesis-construction; strategy C; due_date = today if catalyst < 14 days, else the pre-catalyst window date 7-10 days before the catalyst; context from W1; conservative_default decline). No per-week cap.

E. CROSS-STRATEGY DECONFLICTION — per Strategy.md simultaneous-holding constraints (A↔B and A↔C cannot hold the same name): if a ticker is both a W3 weekly-thesis-action and a W1/W2 new-entry candidate, preserve both idempotent queue entries but add a context note requiring D2 to verify (via the connector / `state.current_positions`) the action disposition before any thesis conversion. Do not predict or stage an exit here.

F. WATCHLIST UPDATES — apply A-queue additions from D, B-watch overflow from C, and any other updates surfaced.

DEFERRAL DISCIPLINE: if a recommendation cannot be acted on this routine, specify (a) trigger date and information source, (b) conservative-default fallback. Deferrals do not chain. Enqueue deferred analyses to the `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue (`events.queue_events`; never the calendar).

CHAT OUTPUT:
- One-line acknowledgment of file edits and idempotent `PENDING_ANALYSIS` queue entries enqueued for D2; no order is crafted by W4.

If no file changes and no queue entries: "No actions required."

ANALYTICS REVIEW (BigQuery) — the Decision_Log live/archive split + weekly prune is RETIRED (`events.decision_log` is queryable + bounded; nothing to archive). Instead:
- **Embedding trend only.** Routine-side `ops.sp_log_decision` embeds inline; pending/error detection and remediation are daily operational concerns. W5 may report the historical weekly embedding-health trend in its outcome, but performs no embedding maintenance.
- Review `analytics.calibration_shrunk` (self-improvement audit S-2/B-2, 2026-07-03 — supersedes reading `analytics.calibration_summary` alone) — per-conviction-tier `win_rate_shrunk` (Beta-Binomial posterior, honest-wide at low N) + `wilson_low`/`wilson_high` + `trustworthy_edge`. Log a one-line note to `events.decision_log` of the current per-tier posterior + interval width; this is the calibration signal any future thesis-construction session should read, NOT the raw `win_rate` column (which reads 1.000 on a small all-wins tier and is the exact overfitting hazard the foundation doc warns against). The BQML `conviction_model` (bigquery/04_analytics.sql, gated at ≥30 closed) is DEPRECATED — a logistic fit on ~30 fee-dominated, single-class, non-independent (one regime, correlated) binary outcomes with 4 categorical features and no CV/walk-forward would overfit; `calibration_shrunk` dominates it and needs no both-classes precondition. Do not build or gate on the BQML model even once 30 closed trades accrue.
- **Historical reconciliation reporting only.** Summarize week-over-week reconciliation/NAV history for learning and trend context, but do not diagnose a live discrepancy, raise an operational drift alert, or attempt a repair. D2a's daily broker reconciliation and its daily monitors are the sole operational owners of current account drift.
- **WASH-SALE EXPOSURE REVIEW (self-improvement audit ITEM 18, 2026-07-11).** **BACK-DATED PARK ROWS — ONE-TIME FULL SWEEP (2026-08-18).** `bigquery/178_park_wash_sale_exposure.sql` extends this view to cover park (`close_strategy='PARK'`) round trips, which were structurally invisible to it before (park fills live in `events.parking_events`, never in `events.trade_fills`). Those rows arrive ALREADY BACK-DATED — the first real one is the 2026-07-27 VOO liquidation, ~$78 of loss repurchased 2026-08-04 — so the "dated since the last W5 run" filter below would skip every one of them forever and this fix would land in the table without ever reaching the operator. Therefore: on the first W5 run that sees ANY `close_strategy='PARK'` row, ignore the date filter for park rows specifically and report the FULL park history once, then revert to the normal since-last-run behaviour (mechanically self-terminating: once reported, the prior `wash-sale-review` decision_log entry names those `close_trade_id`s, so a later run can tell already-reported park rows from genuinely new ones and must report only the latter). Read `state.wash_sale_exposure` (`bigquery/41_tax_lots.sql`, extended by `bigquery/178`) for any exposure rows dated since the last W5 run — a BUY within 30 calendar days of any strategy's loss-realizing SELL in the same ticker, ACROSS strategies (the roster's `n_max=8` ceiling means this experiment deliberately runs multiple strategies that can independently trade the same name; a per-strategy view cannot see this). Log a one-line note to `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='wash-sale-review'`) summarizing new-since-last-run exposure rows (ticker, strategies involved, estimated disallowed-loss amount); if any row is new since the last W5 run, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','wash_sale_exposure','<ticker> wash-sale exposure across strategies <strategies> — see payload for the estimated disallowed amount','<JSON>')` — **the template previously named the "estimated disallowed amount" as message content, contradicting this same bullet's own next sentence; corrected 2026-08-31 (message-stability class sweep) so the template and the rule below it finally agree** so it reaches the monitored alert channel. **`_once`, not the plain `sp_raise_alert` this step used until 2026-08-25.** The step's self-termination guarantee rested entirely on a future memoryless session correctly diffing the prior cycle's `close_trade_id`s out of its own report; with the plain raise there was no dedup backstop if that prose-following ever slipped, and a duplicate exposure alert would simply be inserted. Keep the varying dollar amounts in the JSON payload and the message text stable per `(ticker, strategies)`, since `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on the exact `(category, message)` text. **RENDERING PINNED 2026-09-07: “stable per `(ticker, strategies)`” only holds once `<strategies>` has ONE spelling.** Render it as the DISTINCT strategy codes appearing in that ticker’s reported rows — the union of `close_strategy` and `replacement_strategy` — sorted ASCENDING, joined by a single comma with NO spaces. The 2026-09-07 raise was a single-element set (`PARK`) and so was stable by luck; a two-strategy set has two orderings and only one of them matches the already-open row. Same pin, same reason, as the `regime_restore_shortfall` bullet below. Detection/reporting only — this never blocks a trade or a kill-trigger action (IBKR's own 1099-B, computed off the elected cost-basis method, remains the authoritative tax figure); it exists so the accumulating disallowed-loss exposure is visible before year-end rather than discovered on the 1099-B. **CLOSING THE PRIOR RUN'S NOTICE (added 2026-09-07, alongside the capital-review heal below — this category had no closer either, and for a subtly different reason worth stating so nobody "fixes" it the wrong way).** `wash_sale_exposure` is a **NOTICE, not a condition.** `state.wash_sale_exposure` is a historical record over realized closes and their replacement buys; a wash sale that occurred stays in the view permanently and the view never empties. So there is no condition-cleared moment to wait for, and a heal keyed on the exposure disappearing — the shape used for the two capital categories below — would wait forever and is the wrong instrument here. The alert's actual job is "there is exposure you have not been told about yet", and that job is DONE once this step has written its `wash-sale-review` entry to `events.decision_log`. Therefore, AFTER that entry is written: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'notice delivered: the exposure rows were reported in the events.decision_log wash-sale-review entry for <this run date> (closed by W5)' WHERE category = 'wash_sale_exposure' AND NOT resolved AND alert_ts < <this run's start timestamp>`. **The `alert_ts` bound is load-bearing:** without it this statement closes the alert THIS run has just raised, in the same run, and the operator never sees it — resolve only rows that predate this run, so every notice gets one full weekly cycle on the board. **REGISTRY GAP, closed in-band (same date).** This category has no `ops.alert_policy` row at all — `bigquery/164` registered the three capital categories and nothing ever registered this one, so its latching semantics and closure rule were undeclared for its whole life and a triage session reading the registry would find nothing. Rather than land a one-row SQL file, register it on the first run that finds it missing, with the same `WHERE NOT EXISTS` guard `bigquery/164` uses so it is idempotent and safe to re-run: `INSERT INTO ops.alert_policy (category, latching, resolve_rule, note) SELECT 'wash_sale_exposure', FALSE, 'Closed by W5 on the run AFTER the one that raised it, once the wash-sale-review entry naming the exposure rows has been written to events.decision_log. NOT condition-healed: state.wash_sale_exposure is a permanent historical record that never empties, so an absence test would never fire.', 'Cross-strategy wash-sale exposure: a BUY within 30 calendar days of a loss-realizing SELL in the same ticker, across strategies and including PARK round trips (bigquery/178, bigquery/219). WARNING, never critical - detection and reporting only, it never blocks a trade, and IBKR 1099-B remains the authoritative tax figure.' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ops.alert_policy e WHERE e.category = 'wash_sale_exposure')`.
- Review `analytics.process_scorecard` (self-improvement audit S-7/B-9, 2026-07-03) — decision-quality signals that accrue per-decision, not per rare close: `conviction_tiers_observed` / `analytics.conviction_monotonicity` (does higher stated conviction rank-order higher realized P&L — read as raw per-tier counts, directional only, never a trigger), `go_minus_opened` (a large gap between GO theses and positions actually opened flags a staging-pipeline issue worth a look), and `forecast_pct_below_band` (is the M5 TWR forecast systematically biased — advisory only, per bigquery/06_forecast.sql). Each metric carries its own `min_n_met` floor; below it, log the observation but do not treat it as signal. AUTONOMOUS ROUTING (rev 2026-07-10 — round-2 conversion): a detected staging-pipeline gap must NOT dead-end as a chat note a human is expected to "take a look" at. For any metric with `min_n_met=TRUE` whose reading is out of band (e.g. `go_minus_opened` materially positive), log the finding to `events.decision_log` AND `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','W5','process_scorecard_signal','<metric + value + strategy>','<JSON>')` so it reaches the monitored alert channel rather than an unread chat surface (severity bumped info→warning 2026-07-16, consumption-closure CC-7 — `info` is filtered by both `alert_emailer.gs` and `alert_relay.py`, so this alert never actually reached any monitored channel until now); `forecast_pct_below_band` stays advisory (log-only) per bigquery/06_forecast.sql.
- **CAPITAL-UTILISATION & RESTORE-INTEGRITY REVIEW (2026-08-11, `bigquery/164_capital_utilisation_and_restore_integrity.sql`).** Three read-only checks on whether the capital model is still doing what Experiment_Parameters.md says it does — reward winners passively via survivorship. All three are WARNING-class and none can halt trading.

  **HEAL FIRST, FROM THIS SAME READ, BEFORE YOU RAISE (added 2026-09-07 — the exact sibling of D2a's regime/nomadic heal added the day before, found because `regime_restore_shortfall` fired on 2026-09-07 with nothing anywhere able to close it).** `bigquery/164` registered all three of these categories `latching = FALSE`, each with a `resolve_rule` opening "Auto-resolves when …" — and W5, the only routine that reads these views, implemented ONLY the raise side. Nothing else can close them: `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts` is hardcoded to an unrelated category set and touches none of the three, and no other routine reads `state.capital_utilisation_watch` or `state.regime_restore_shortfall_risk` at all. So a condition that healed weeks ago still sits on the board as an open WARNING — and since `state.system_health.open_alerts` counts every unresolved row and the emailer re-lists the board, it becomes permanent weekly noise: exactly the alarm fatigue this plan warns about, arriving through a promise the registry made and no code kept. **Evaluate the heal from the SAME read that drives the raise, ABOVE the branch**, per ONE MOVEMENT PER READ — a second `SELECT` can observe a different snapshot and close a row the raise branch is about to re-open.
  - **`capital_stranded` — heal PER STRATEGY, never category-wide.** This is the one place D2a's pattern must NOT be copied verbatim. D2a may scope its heal by `category` alone because `sp_raise_alert_once` admits at most one open row per category *when the message is constant*; here the message deliberately names the strategy (see item 1 below), so this category holds **one open row PER STRATEGY**, and a category-wide `UPDATE` would close strategy B's live alert the moment strategy A deploys — silently destroying a true warning. For each strategy present in the rows you just read with `is_stranded = FALSE`: `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'condition healed: state.capital_utilisation_watch no longer reports is_stranded for this strategy — it deployed, was evaluated again, or its idle capital fell below the floor (healed by W5)' WHERE category = 'capital_stranded' AND NOT resolved AND STARTS_WITH(message, '<strategy> has stranded idle capital')`. Match on the STRATEGY-BEARING PREFIX rather than the whole literal: the prefix carries the identity, and a prefix match still finds a row raised under an earlier wording of the tail.
  - **`regime_restore_shortfall` — heal on the FLAGS, never on an empty result.** `state.regime_restore_shortfall_risk` is `FROM donors CROSS JOIN newcomer LEFT JOIN debt ON TRUE`, and `bigquery/164`'s own header states the consequence outright: "This shape always emits at least one row: a single all-clear row with `strategy = NULL` when no debt exists, and one row per debtor otherwise." That shape is deliberate — a monitor that goes silent when healthy is indistinguishable from one that has died — so an absence test here is not merely fragile, it is **unreachable**: it would never fire, and the heal would be vacuous. Heal only when the rows you just read carry `aggregate_at_risk = FALSE` **AND** `at_risk_including_newcomer_claim = FALSE` (both, since either one alone raises): `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'condition healed: donor capacity again covers the outstanding regime-capital debt including the pending-newcomer claim (healed by W5)' WHERE category = 'regime_restore_shortfall' AND NOT resolved`. Category-wide scope is correct HERE and only here: the raise is an aggregate condition over the whole book, so the pinned message admits exactly one open row.
  - **`capital_concentration` — nothing to heal, and that is not a defect.** `bigquery/164` registered it but, as its own note records, it is "not wired to a raise call on apply — reserved for a future D3/W5 step". Nothing raises it, so nothing can be open. Do NOT add a heal for it, and do NOT read its registered-but-unraised state as the same defect as the two above. **`cash_fee` (`bigquery/214`) is in the identical position** — verified 2026-09-07: no `sp_raise_alert` site anywhere names it, so its resolve_rule naming no routine costs nothing. **The general rule for a no-closer sweep: check whether anything RAISES the category before calling its missing closer a defect.** A registered-but-unwired category is a reserved slot, not a leak; only a category that can actually open a row needs a path to close it.
  1. `SELECT * FROM state.capital_utilisation_watch` — one row per capital-ENABLED strategy. For any row with `is_stranded = TRUE`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','capital_stranded','<strategy> has stranded idle capital — see payload for the idle amount and days since deployment','<TO_JSON_STRING of the row>')`. **MESSAGE STABILITY, corrected 2026-08-31 (message-stability class sweep): the template here named `idle_capital` and `days_since_deployment` as MESSAGE content, and both drift every week the condition persists — `idle_capital` with marks, `days_since_deployment` by construction. `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on `WHERE NOT resolved AND category = in_category AND message = in_message` (`bigquery/10_observability.sql`), an EXACT string match and nothing else, so a drifting message degenerates `_once` into a plain `sp_raise_alert` and a persisting stranded strategy raises a FRESH weekly alert, each separately emailed. Keep the strategy code — constant for the life of the condition, so it correctly gives one open row PER strategy — and carry every varying number in the payload.** Same rule and same reason as the `wash_sale_exposure` bullet above and the `probe_funding_stalled` correction in SL3 STEP 5 (2026-08-26). **Read the `posture` column before acting.** A strategy that is idle but has a non-zero `evaluations_60d` is HEALTHY — Operating_Protocols §16 says an active strategy that is merely idle keeps its capital, and declining a thesis on its own mechanical criteria IS the strategy working. `is_stranded` deliberately fires only when idle capital is material AND there has been no deployment for 90+ days AND nothing has evaluated the strategy in 60 days. Do NOT widen this predicate to "idle capital alone"; it would fire on every healthy low-frequency strategy from day one and be muted within a week.
  2. `SELECT * FROM state.regime_restore_shortfall_risk` — the swept-capital debt against what the enabled donors could actually return. On `aggregate_at_risk` or `at_risk_including_newcomer_claim`, `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5','regime_restore_shortfall','debtors <strategy-codes> — swept-capital debt exceeds returnable donor capacity; see payload for total debt, donor capacity and shortfall','<JSON>')`. **MESSAGE STABILITY, corrected 2026-08-31 (message-stability class sweep): the template named three DOLLAR figures as message content. This passage itself says `bigquery/98`'s restore trigger is "a standing condition … re-evaluated on every read, no transition gate, no cooldown" — so those figures move on every W5 evaluation while the same underlying under-capitalisation persists, and `sp_raise_alert_once`'s exact-message dedup therefore never matches. Name only the identifiers in the message; the dollars belong in the payload.** **RENDERING PINNED 2026-09-07 — the same class, third pass, found because this alert fired.** “Name only the identifiers” left HOW to name them to the session, and a memoryless routine composes that clause fresh every week: the 2026-09-07 raise rendered it `debtor strategies A, B and D against an empty enabled-donor set` — a sentence no second session reproduces byte-for-byte. That is the same `_once`-defeating drift as a moving dollar figure, arriving through PROSE instead of arithmetic, and nothing in the fleet can see it: `bigquery/205` swept moving VALUES, `bigquery/227` swept `STRING_AGG` ORDERING, and `scripts/check_alert_message_stability.py` parses `bigquery/*.sql` — none of the three looks at a template whose message is rendered by a ROUTINE rather than by SQL. The message is now a FIXED literal with exactly ONE substitution: `<strategy-codes>` is the DISTINCT non-NULL `strategy` values of the rows you just read, sorted ASCENDING, joined by a single comma with NO spaces, and nothing else — no prose, no donor-set clause, no counts, no “and”. Donor capacity moves independently of the debtor set, so naming it in the message would re-introduce exactly the drift this pin removes; it belongs in the payload only. **Read "shortfall" as THIS SESSION'S shortfall, not a loss.** `bigquery/98`'s restore trigger is a standing condition (any enabled strategy with `outstanding_debt > 0`, re-evaluated on every read, no transition gate, no cooldown, no retry guard), so an unpaid residual is re-proposed automatically as donor capacity recovers — the `>=$25-or-full-debt` floor only defers a sub-$25 tail, it cannot strand it. So this alert means "a re-enabled strategy is trading on a fraction of its owed capital right now," not "capital was lost." That is still worth surfacing, because an under-capitalised debtor is otherwise invisible — it just quietly trades smaller than it should, and nobody would connect that to a sweep weeks earlier. The view also nets the SISA pending-newcomer probe-stake claim, because newcomers outrank the restore on every inflow and nothing else shows the two claims against one pool.
  3. `SELECT * FROM state.sweep_recipient_weights` — informational this run. It precomputes the mechanical, judgment-free capacity tilt (share of the trailing 180 days each recipient actually held a position, mapped onto §16's sanctioned [0.5x, 2x] band) that a future D2a SWEEP substep may apply instead of DEFAULT-EQUAL. No alert; log the reading if `sweep_share` diverges materially from `equal_share`, since that is the first evidence the tilt would change an outcome.
- **EXTERNAL-SPEND DIGEST (2026-08-17, `bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql` — the consumer that closes the shared "Metered external calls" rule's part (d)).** Read BOTH: `SELECT * FROM state.web_spend_month WHERE month_start >= DATE_TRUNC(DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Denver'), INTERVAL 60 DAY), MONTH)` (per `(month, provider, routine)` call counts and credits) **and `SELECT * FROM state.web_duplicate_targets ORDER BY credits_on_repeats DESC LIMIT 25`** — both over `ops.web_calls`. Log one `events.decision_log` entry via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with `entry_type='external-spend-digest'`, naming the current month's fleet total per provider, the top 3 routines by `credits`, and — **the finding that actually matters** — the top repeat-fetched targets with their `credits_on_repeats` and whether each is `is_cross_routine`. **A cross-routine repeat is the highest-value one to report**: neither routine can see the other doing it, so it is the class that persists indefinitely unnoticed, and it is the concrete instance of the shared rule's "the one thing that IS waste." **ALSO NAME THE PRICED-DEPTH SHARE, which this digest has never reported even though the column already exists (added 2026-08-21, external-spend audit).** `state.web_spend_month` already computes `n_priced_upgrade` (`bigquery/174_web_call_telemetry.sql`) and nothing has ever read it, so the second of the two levers the shared rule's baseline note itself names — "search COUNT and search DEPTH, in that order" — is measured, stored, and then left out of the only report that reads this table. Per `(month, routine)`, state `n_priced_upgrade` as a share of that routine's Tavily searches together with the credits attributable to the upgrade (advanced bills 2 credits to basic's 1, so the upgrade's own cost in credits equals `n_priced_upgrade`), and say when that share MOVED rather than only where it stands: measured across the 171 logged Tavily calls to 2026-08-21, 95 were advanced (55.6%) = 95 of 252.4 logged credits, **38% of logged Tavily spend**, and the rate swung from 14% advanced on the 2026-08-19 D1 run (8 of 57 searches) to 76% on 2026-08-20 (54 of 71) across two consecutive runs with no recorded reason — the swing is the reportable finding, not the level. Same FLOOR caveat as (1) below: this share is computed over LOGGED calls only. **RECORD-ONLY — no threshold, no alert, no cap; nothing here gates anything and W5 never edits a token. Specifically, this share is NOT a proposal to disable `auto_parameters=true` or to force basic depth** — that setting is ENDORSED by owner directive 2026-08-17 (the session picks depth per task, paying 2 credits when that is the better answer), and a depth cap read out of this number would be exactly the unfounded knob the "no per-routine credit cap from spend alone" rule below refuses. Two honesty requirements, both binding: (1) **report `has_unreported_runs`** — where TRUE, that routine logged completed runs that emitted no token, so its credits are a **FLOOR, not a total**; name those routines rather than quoting a fleet figure that reads as complete; (2) per the shared rule this series is a **self-reported ESTIMATE, not a meter** (no usage endpoint exists on the Tavily MCP surface), so the provider's own dashboard stays authoritative for the account total — state the estimate as an estimate and never reconcile the two silently. **Do not propose a per-routine credit cap from fewer than two COMPLETE months of tokens.** The series exists precisely to make such a cap evidence-based; a first partial month is the noise the sibling process-reliability loop's 3-consecutive-cycle persistence bar exists to reject, and the same discipline binds here.
- **SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE (added 2026-08-28 — W5 is the named owner on most of these and, until now, read none of them).**
  `SELECT alert_id, alert_ts, source, category, message, payload FROM ops.alerts WHERE severity = 'info' AND NOT resolved ORDER BY alert_ts`.
  These are cross-surface findings other routines recorded under the shared **OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS** rule
  (§Observability) — a routine found a defect on a surface it does not own and filed it rather than fixing it.
  **This step exists because the venue had no consumer at all.** Measured 2026-08-28: 12 open `info` rows,
  8 of them naming "W5 self-improvement" as the nearest owning routine, and W5's section contained ZERO reads of
  `ops.alerts` — every one of those rows was stranded by construction, some for days, and the fleet had begun
  independently rediscovering the same defects and filing the rediscoveries into the same void. That is the exact
  failure the rule now warns about, so W5 must not recreate it: the point of this step is that these rows get
  ADJUDICATED, not merely listed in a digest.
  For each row, do ONE of three things and say which:
  1. **FIX IT** if the surface is W5's own or the fix is a self-contained prose/spec correction W5 can make in this
     run. Then `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = '<what
     changed, with the file and named anchor>' WHERE alert_id = '<id>'` — scope by `alert_id`, never by category.
  2. **ROUTE IT** if a lane with a real drainer fits (`PENDING_ANALYSIS`→D2, `PENDING_REVIEW`→AR_att/AR_orc,
     `PENDING_DRAFT`→SL2, `PENDING_ROSTER`→SL5): write the queue row, then resolve the alert citing the
     `item_key` you created. Confirm the drainer really reads that lane before claiming it — the same
     verified-consumer obligation the shared rule states, and what `state.queue_venue_claim_unwired` checks
     mechanically.
  3. **REJECT IT** if it is not a real defect, is already fixed, or is superseded. Resolve with the evidence that
     shows so. A rejection needs a reason a later reader can check, not an assertion.
  Leave a row OPEN only when it genuinely needs an owner decision W5 cannot make; say so in this run's note and
  name what is blocked. **Never resolve one merely to clear the board** — an unactioned resolve is worse than the
  strand it replaces, because it destroys the record too. These categories are deliberately absent from
  `ops.alert_policy`'s auto-resolve allowlist so they latch until someone acts; do not add them to it.
  **ESCALATE A ROW LEFT OPEN ACROSS >=2 CONSECUTIVE CYCLES (added 2026-09-08, run-outcome notification design
  P6(d)).** A row correctly left OPEN above reaches no channel at all: `info` severity is filtered out of both
  `alert_emailer.gs` and `alert_relay.py` (measured: 104 of 104 `info` alerts raised in the trailing 90d were
  never delivered), and every one of the 33 live triggers routes its OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS into exactly this
  venue via the SCOPE_ADDENDUM — the same class CC-7 already fixed once for `immediate_action_flagged` /
  `process_scorecard_signal` (info→warning, 2026-07-16). For each row left OPEN this cycle, check whether
  `alert_ts < <the previous completed W5 run's log_ts>` (`SELECT MAX(log_ts) FROM ops.run_log WHERE
  routine='W5' AND status='completed' AND log_ts < <this run's start>`): since this step reads every open
  `info` row unconditionally every W5 cycle, a row whose `alert_ts` predates the last completed W5 run was
  necessarily read and left open on that prior cycle too, so this predicate alone proves >=2 consecutive
  cycles open with no separate counter to maintain. On that row: `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('warning','W5',
  'spec_defect_notice_stalled', '<alert_id> has sat OPEN in SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE for >=2 consecutive W5
  cycles and needs an owner decision', '<JSON: alert_id, category, source, first_seen_open_at>')`. **The
  message's only variable is the underlying row's `alert_id`, stable for the life of that row (C2) — never
  embed the cycle count or a date, both of which would re-mint a fresh alert every week this stays open.**
  HEAL: whenever this step FIXes, ROUTEs, or REJECTs a row above (resolving it), also `UPDATE ops.alerts SET
  resolved = TRUE, resolved_ts = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note = 'underlying alert_id resolved: <FIX/
  ROUTE/REJECT and how>' WHERE category = 'spec_defect_notice_stalled' AND NOT resolved AND JSON_VALUE(payload,
  '$.alert_id') = '<the alert_id just resolved>'` — the escalation's closure path is exactly its parent row's
  closure, so it needs no separate auto-age entry.

- **PROCESS-RELIABILITY REVIEW (self-improvement audit WO-6, 2026-07-03; active_auto per `ops/autonomy_levels.yaml`, loop `process_reliability`; rev 2026-07-10b — stage bumped to match ceiling, code-review finding #7, owner-confirmed. The loop's OWN data-sufficiency gate below — not a separate stage check — governs whether it does anything on a given firing).** First, the ALWAYS-autonomous fail-safe check (unconditional, runs before anything else in this bullet): read `state.process_constant_oos_watch` (bigquery/72_constant_tuning_oos_watch.sql); for any `degraded_revert = TRUE` row, auto-REVERT the constant to `old_value` (edit the version-controlled deadline/threshold back, run `check_cadence_consistency.py`, commit + push, auto-merge on green CI), `INSERT` an `ops.process_constant_change_log` row with `change_key = CONCAT(<original change_key>, ':REVERT')` (and the same routine/deadline_key, old/new swapped), log `events.decision_log`, and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','W5','process_constant_reverted','<routine + deadline_key + restored value + post-change threat evidence>','<JSON>')` — a post-change threat recurrence means the relaxation was chasing a drifting routine; restoring the tighter deadline is the fail-safe direction (the watchdog alarms instead of being quietly loosened). Then read `analytics.routine_health_scorecard` (canonical definition bigquery/89 as of 2026-07-18, superseding bigquery/27): per-routine 90-day completion/failure/halt counts, p50/p90 completion minutes (midnight-safe as of bigquery/89 — computed as minutes since 00:00 of `run_date`, so a past-midnight completion reads >1440 instead of wrapping to near-zero), dep-gate abort count, and the retry-telemetry columns (`n_retry_events`, `n_retries_exhausted`, `n_dep_waits`, `n_dep_wait_futile`, `n_active_refires`, `total_wait_minutes` — from `state.retry_telemetry`, bigquery/88).   BOTH notification paths (`scripts/alert_relay.py` and `alert_emailer.gs` each take
  `severity IN ('critical','warning')`) and would never reach the operator — which is the one thing
  this step exists to prevent. **CLOSURE PATH, so the row cannot latch open forever:** it is resolved
  by the owner-facing re-evaluation itself — a `events.decision_log` row with
  `entry_type='park-ladder-reevaluation'` recording the verdict (continue / retune / demote to shadow
  / abandon). Until that row exists the alert legitimately stays open and keeps re-notifying, which is
  the intended behaviour for a decision the owner has asked to be forced back to.
  **What the re-evaluating session must NOT do:** treat 3 episodes as a significance test. Measured
  before activation over 15 historical episodes, forward-looking with the execution lag, the defensive
  signal had mean edge −0.638pp with SD 1.308pp and won only 4 of 15 — SD is ~2x the effect, so
  resolving it statistically needs ~30 episodes (~2.5 years), not three. The forward test is for
  STRUCTURAL discovery (does the shock axis fire on real risk or on cross-asset noise; does STRICT
  decay hold f too long), and the decision-relevant criterion is `ladder_edge_vs_actual_pp` — the
  alternative to the ladder is the binary all-or-nothing switch, not never de-risking.
  `mean_edge_vs_never_pp` is reported alongside because whether to de-risk AT ALL is a real and larger
  question, but it does not gate this one.

**NO-GO COUNTERFACTUAL SHADOW-TRACKING (self-improvement audit S-3, 2026-07-03) — makes step 3 above bidirectional.** The taxonomy above records only avoided trades; it never checks whether the avoided name actually underperformed, which is pure survivorship/confirmation-bias exposure. Two sub-steps, both best-effort (a connector hiccup must never abort W5). **Price sourcing (rewired 2026-07-19: IBKR-primary after FMP free-tier re-scope; owner-approved):** IBKR is PRIMARY — resolve the shadow ticker via `search_contracts` (exact-symbol row, US primary listing) and read `get_price_snapshot`'s `last` (when the market is closed, `last`/`prior_close` is the prior close — fine for a weekly shadow mark); `mcp__FMP__quote` is a best-effort FALLBACK only, and now works only for FMP's free-list symbols (~87 big-caps + 9 indexes) since FMP's 2026-07-19 free-tier re-scoping symbol-blocked the rest:

The raw-grain summary view is kept, unchanged, for the finer per-composite detail. Also check `n_closed_unscored`: a NON-ZERO value there means closed rows whose excess return could not be computed, which is the failure mode that hid the 2026-07-19..2026-08-09 outage (a NULL scored in neither direction and read as "no signal yet" rather than "never scored") — investigate it rather than reading the tally as complete. For any sub-pattern with `min_n_met = TRUE` (>=5 closed-out) and `n_incorrect > n_correct`, append a note to that sub-pattern's B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md section: "counterfactual tally: X/Y NO-GOs where the avoided name subsequently underperformed SGOV — below-chance, candidate for taxonomy review" — an autonomously-actioned taxonomy update, NOT a chat/human-visible flag someone must resolve (rev 2026-07-10 — round-2 conversion). The N-floor caveat is PRESERVED as the data gate: a below-chance tally at low N can still be noise, so while `5 <= N < 20` the note above stays informational-only and routing is NOT down-weighted. Once a sub-pattern reaches **N >= 20** closed-out shadow rows still with `n_incorrect > n_correct`, the loop SELF-APPLIES the down-weight with NO human taxonomy-review step: change that note to a dated `DEMOTED — routing down-weighted` entry, commit + push (auto-merge on green CI), log an `events.decision_log` entry, and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','W5','nogo_subpattern_demoted','<sub-pattern + X/Y tally>','<JSON>')`.

**THE UPPER BOUND IS PINNED AT 20, RESOLVING THE PRIOR `15-20` RANGE (W5 2026-08-30).** This clause read `N>=15-20` on both sides of the partition from its authoring until 2026-08-30, which is not a threshold but a range — and because both clauses used the identical token, a token landing anywhere inside [15, 20] belonged to neither branch and to both. That went unnoticed for as long as no token had ever crossed 15. On 2026-08-30 SP4 closed out at **N=17 (5 correct / 12 incorrect)** — the first token ever to enter the range — and W5 had to adjudicate a SELF-APPLY, with no human step, on prose that did not determine the answer. It is pinned at the CONSERVATIVE end because that is the end the clause's own stated rationale points to: the caveat exists to avoid down-weighting on noise, so where the text is ambiguous the reading that declines to act is the one consistent with its purpose. Concretely, at n=17 with 5 correct the one-sided binomial p under a fair-coin null is **0.072** — above the conventional bar, i.e. the noise this gate guards against is demonstrably not yet excluded at the range's lower end. Do NOT re-open this as a range; if the bar should move, move the number.

**REPORT THE MARGINAL TRANCHE, NOT ONLY THE CUMULATIVE TALLY — binding whenever a token is at or near the bar.** A cumulative below-chance count says nothing about whether the evidence is still arriving in that direction, and the difference decides the action. Measured on 2026-08-30: SP4's cumulative reading was 5/17 (below chance, in-band) while the SEVEN rows that closed that very cycle went **4 correct / 3 incorrect** — above chance — moving the cumulative from 1/10 (10%) to 5/17 (29%). A session reading only the cumulative number would have seen a token marching toward demotion; the tranche shows its fresh evidence had just reversed. So whenever this step reports a tally for a token with `min_n_met = TRUE`, state (i) the cumulative `n_correct`/`n_closed_out`, (ii) the count and direction of the rows closed THIS cycle, and (iii) whether those two agree — and if the marginal tranche contradicts the cumulative direction, say so and do not treat the cumulative figure as a trend. This is a REPORTING requirement, not a second gate: it never blocks a self-apply that the N>=20 bar authorizes, it only forbids reaching that bar without having looked.

**DECISION-LOG VOCABULARY DRIFT WATCH (added 2026-07-30, decision-record audit).** W5 already owns controlled-vocabulary hygiene for `sub_pattern` (ops/RUNBOOK.md §21 — the one sanctioned in-place-UPDATE exception, and W5 conforms any drift). Extend that ownership to the two columns the learning views actually key on, which had NO owner and no check at all. This is a ROUTINE-side watch by necessity, not a CI gate: this repo's CI checkers are static offline text parsers with no live BigQuery access (only the keyless-WIF `warehouse-validation` job touches the warehouse), so nothing in CI can see a bad value that only exists as data.

Query the vocabulary actually in use since the last W5 run:

```sql
SELECT entry_type, decision, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(entry_date) AS first_seen, MAX(entry_date) AS last_seen
FROM `stock-trading-498512.events.decision_log`
WHERE entry_date > <last W5 run date>
GROUP BY entry_type, decision ORDER BY n DESC
```

Check BOTH DIRECTIONS. Checking only one is how the 2026-07-20..22 incident stayed invisible for months:

**(a) WRONGLY EXCLUDED (false negative)** — a value not in the controlled vocabulary, which a view's filter therefore drops. This is the entry_type='thesis' case.

**(b) WRONGLY INCLUDED (false positive)** — a value that a view's filter MATCHES but that is not in the sanctioned set. This direction exists because `analytics.thesis_outcomes.is_go_family` is a `^GO\b` PREFIX test, which is strictly more permissive than the two-value GO family it is meant to recognise: verified live that `'GO/NO-GO'`, `'GO-WITHOUT-ORDER'`, `'GO-AHEAD'`, `'GO,'` and `'GO (partial)'` would all match. Any of those would be counted as a GO observation in calibration AND would pass the campaign-join guard that exists to stop a non-GO thesis inheriting a real position's realized P&L. Run:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT decision FROM `stock-trading-498512.events.decision_log`
WHERE entry_type IN ('thesis-construction','thesis')
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(decision,''))), r'^GO\b')
  AND UPPER(TRIM(decision)) NOT IN ('GO', 'GO (ADD TRANCHE)')
```

Any row returned is a false positive already accruing into calibration — treat as CRITICAL, not a warning, and tighten `is_go_family` to an explicit allowlist in a new numbered `bigquery/` file in the same session.

For any value found in EITHER direction: **do not attempt to UPDATE the rows** (append-only; only `sub_pattern` has an exception, and a second standing exception was explicitly declined — ops/RUNBOOK.md §44). Instead, in the same W5 session: (i) determine whether any learning view's filter silently excludes it — check `analytics.thesis_outcomes`, `analytics.conviction_features`, `analytics.thesis_outcome_summary` for the affected row; (ii) if it IS excluded, widen the relevant view's synonym tolerance in a NEW numbered `bigquery/` file, apply it live, and mirror the change into the dbt model so the dbt-parity row-level check stays green; (iii) correct the emitting routine's text here so the drift stops at source; (iv) `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('info','W5','decision_vocab_drift','<the value + affected view>','<JSON>')` and log it in the W5 outcome entry. Self-executed, no chat step.

WHY this is worth a weekly query: the 2026-07-20..22 `entry_type='thesis'` incident ran for three days, self-corrected, and was never noticed — it took a dedicated audit four months later to find that a real Strategy B GO had been invisible to every calibration view the whole time. `analytics.thesis_outcomes.paired_by_fk` and the drift query above are the two cheap telemetry reads that would have surfaced it in a week.

Two output files:

OUTPUT 1 — **write the structured macro indicators to `events.macro_series`** (one row per metric per release; the `Monthly_Macro_Data_*.md` audit file is RETIRED 2026-06-06 per Operating_Protocols §15 — do NOT recreate it). These are the audit trail of underlying inputs, NOT read by M1b. **Also append EVERY covered month's new prints to `events.macro_fred`** — the deep-history macro substrate that M5's `AI.FORECAST` reads — backfilling all missed months, not only the immediately-prior one, so M5 never inherits a silent forecast-substrate gap. **Pull via the FMP connector first** (`mcp__FMP__economics` `treasury-rates` + `economics-indicators`; map + YoY transforms in bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql §refresh), since the remote routine has FMP but may lack outbound `curl`; fall back to the FRED public CSV (no key) for any series FMP doesn't carry (notably `hy_oas`). Tag each row `source='FMP'` or `'FRED'`.

  **THE FIVE DAILY→MONTH-END METRICS NEED A PINNED DATE — never take "latest" for any of them (rule added 2026-08-05 after the defect below).** Most metrics here are monthly-native (CPI, PPI, payrolls, U-3, `fed_funds`, …) and cannot suffer this bug. Exactly five are DAILY series collapsed to a month-end level per `bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql:40-44` + line 76 ("the last VALID obs in the month, dated first-of-month") — **`vix`, `treasury_10y`, `treasury_2y`, `yield_curve_10y2y`, `hy_oas`** — and every one of them must be read for a SPECIFIC date: the covered month's **last trading day**. Resolve that date first, then:
  - **`vix`** — `SELECT close FROM state.signal_marks_curated WHERE ticker = '^VIX' AND mark_date = <that date>`. D2a STEP 1d ingests this daily and it is already correctly dated. Tag `source='FMP'`. Backfilling a missed month works the same way; the series carries ≥1y of history.
  - **`treasury_10y` / `treasury_2y`** — `mcp__FMP__economics` `treasury-rates` **with `from_date`/`to_date` both pinned to that date** (verified 2026-08-05: this endpoint returns explicitly dated rows, so it is safe *only* when you pass the date — an unpinned call returns the latest row and reintroduces the bug). Read `year10` / `year2`. Tag `source='FMP'`.
  - **`yield_curve_10y2y`** — the 10Y−2Y spread from the same pinned `treasury-rates` row, i.e. `.year10 − .year2` of the row you just read. **Be clear about what this does and does not verify (corrected 2026-08-06 — the rule as first written claimed a cross-check that was tautological).** Deriving the spread from the same row makes it consistent WITH those legs *by construction*: comparing it back to `treasury_10y − treasury_2y` is A−B against A−B and can never fail, so it provides ZERO verification. What actually guarantees this metric is correct is the DATE-PINNING of the `treasury-rates` call itself — that is the control, not any subsequent arithmetic check. **Optional genuine cross-check, when reachable:** FRED publishes `T10Y2Y` as an independent series (`bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql`); if you can read it for the same pinned date, comparing it to your derived spread IS a real two-source test — a disagreement means one of the two pulls is off-date, so stop and re-resolve. Note `fred.stlouisfed.org` returns HTTP 403 to a direct fetch and needs the Tavily-extract route with a cache-busting query param (see `hy_oas` above), so treat this as best-effort, never a gate. *(Historical note: the 2026-07 defect was exposed by exactly this kind of disagreement — the stored spread 0.47 was right while its own stored legs implied 0.45 — but that was only detectable because the spread had come from FRED's independent T10Y2Y print while the legs came from a stale FMP row. Same-row derivation would have hidden it.)*
  - **`hy_oas`** — FRED `BAMLH0A0HYM2` remains the only source (FMP does not carry it, `bigquery/07_fred_macro.sql:68`; no independent dated credit-spread series exists anywhere in this project). **Require the source to actually contain a row for that date.** If the print is not yet published, write NO `hy_oas` row for the month and backfill it on the next run — never substitute the nearest earlier date silently. **This series publishes with a ~1-day lag and updates around 08:52–11:30 CDT**, so a `first_trading_day` M1a run in the early-morning MT slot will routinely fire BEFORE the month-end print exists — expect the deferred-backfill path to be the NORMAL case here, not an exception. **Fetch note (measured 2026-08-05, REVISED 2026-08-30):** `fred.stlouisfed.org` returns **HTTP 403 to a direct `WebFetch`** (both the `fredgraph.csv` and `/data/*.txt` forms); the series page IS readable via Tavily extract, and a cache-busting query param (e.g. `?cb=<today>`) is needed or a stale crawl comes back. **BUT TAVILY EXTRACT IS NO LONGER RELIABLE HERE, AND IT IS NO LONGER THE ONLY PATH.** D1 measured `Request timed out at 10.02s` against BOTH sanctioned paths (the `fredgraph.csv` endpoint and the series page, each cache-busted) on 2026-08-24 and again on 2026-08-30 — two runs six days apart, four failures, zero successes. Failed extractions are not billed, so this costs evidence, not credits. **MEASURED AGAIN 2026-09-01 (M1a), AND IT SUCCEEDED — so treat the unreliability claim as INTERMITTENT, not settled:** the cache-busted series page returned current data via Tavily extract in 6.21s on the first attempt, and the rung-3 `curl` returned HTTP 200 in 1.56s with the same last observation, both agreeing on `BAMLH0A0HYM2` `2026-08-28,2.60`. Rung 2 is therefore still worth attempting before rung 3 rather than skipped as known-dead; the request-shaped-block hypothesis below is untouched by this (it still explains the `WebFetch` 403), but a blanket "no longer reliable" reading of Tavily is now contradicted by direct measurement. **FRED ITSELF IS UP: a plain `curl` with its DEFAULT User-Agent got HTTP 200 from both paths in under 0.3s, twice each, on 2026-08-30**, returning current data (`BAMLH0A0HYM2` last row `2026-08-27,2.63`). The same host, same session, same machine FAILED every one of four attempts when the request carried a normal browser User-Agent (HTTP/2 `INTERNAL_ERROR`; an 18s dead timeout when forced to HTTP/1.1). **So the block is REQUEST-SHAPED, not availability-shaped** — which fits both the `WebFetch` 403 and the Tavily timeouts, since both present browser-shaped clients. Treat that mechanism as INFERRED, not proven: the successful curl ran from a different network path than Tavily's crawler, so it is strong evidence about FRED's liveness and only suggestive about the cause. **FETCH LADDER — try in this order, and stop at the first that returns a row for the target date:** (1) `mcp__FMP__economics` per OUTPUT 1 above (free, structured, already paid for — but it does NOT carry `hy_oas`, so for THIS series the ladder starts at 2); (2) `tavily_extract` on the series page, cache-busted, as before; (3) **`curl` the public CSV with curl's own default User-Agent and do NOT spoof a browser one** — `curl -sS 'https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=BAMLH0A0HYM2'` — which is the "fall back to the FRED public CSV (no key)" path OUTPUT 1 already names, now with a measured reason the User-Agent matters; it needs no API key and costs nothing. OUTPUT 1's caveat that the remote routine "may lack outbound `curl`" still stands and is why this is rung 3, not rung 1 — if `curl` is unavailable or egress-blocked in the run environment, say so explicitly rather than reporting the series as unavailable. **FETCH FAILURE IS NOT THE SAME EVENT AS AN UNPUBLISHED PRINT, and must not be logged as one.** The deferred-backfill rule above ("write NO `hy_oas` row and backfill on the next run") is for a print FRED has not released yet — a correct, expected, silent outcome. If every rung of the ladder fails, the print may well exist and this run simply could not read it: still write no row, but ALSO `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','M1a','hy_oas_fetch_path_exhausted', ...)` naming each rung and its failure mode. Silently taking the backfill path on a fetch failure is what makes a scored input degrade invisibly, and `hy_oas` is scored here, not merely corroborating. **Month-end nuance specific to this series:** FRED states *"when the last calendar day of the month takes place on the weekend, weekend observations will occur as a result of month ending accrued interest adjustments"* — so for `hy_oas` the month's last valid observation can legitimately be a **Saturday or Sunday date**, unlike the equity and treasury series. Take the last observation IN the month, not the last weekday.
  **Why this rule exists — do not revert it to an unpinned quote/CSV pull.** On 2026-08-03 M1a wrote July's `vix` as **17.09**, which is the **2026-07-30** close; the true 2026-07-31 close was **15.99**. It made the identical error on three more metrics in the same batch — **four of the five were wrong, and only `yield_curve_10y2y` (0.47) was right**: `treasury_10y` **4.68**, `treasury_2y` **4.23** and `hy_oas` **2.84** are all the 07-30 prints verbatim, against true 07-31 values of **4.75**, **4.28** and **2.85** (confirmed 2026-08-05 against date-pinned FMP `treasury-rates` and the FRED series page; all four corrected in `events.macro_fred` that day). That `yield_curve_10y2y` alone survived is the diagnostic worth remembering: its own FRED print had already published, so the stored spread was right while its own stored legs implied 0.45 — **an internally inconsistent set is the cheapest detector for this bug class.** Two independent causes, both structural, neither fixable by "try harder":
  (i) a live `quote` call has **no date argument at all** — it returns the latest close and physically cannot select a historical month-end; and
  (ii) the FRED `VIXCLS` CSV publishes with a lag, and M1a's cadence is `monthly first_trading_day` (`ops/cadence.yaml`), so it fires exactly when the just-closed month's final print is least likely to be posted. This is a **recurring monthly collision**, not a one-off — the same run corrected June to 16.45 (which matches the 06-30 close exactly), so the failure is specifically "the newest print isn't there yet," not a bad transform.
  Consequences that actually landed, as the reason to keep this pinned: the wrong value propagated into `analytics.deployed_twr_forecast` (2026-08-03 vintage, vix path 16.91→17.45→17.58) and produced a **false** "Above band: `vix` 17.09 (+0.41)" calibration breach in M5's `forecast-monitor` `events.decision_log` entry — the true 15.99 sits inside the July vintage's 80% band [13.28, 16.68]. The trading router was never affected (it reads `TECHNICAL_SIGNAL/VIX_REGIME`, computed by D2a from the same dated ingest), which is exactly why routing M1a to that ingest closes the gap. This keeps the macro forecast current without depending on agent-side HTTP. `macro_fred` is a separate bulk/forecast substrate, distinct from this hand-curated `macro_series` audit table:

PART 1 — Coverage of every calendar month since M1a's last successful completion (normally just the prior month; label each covered month explicitly, oldest first). If a section has no material items for a given month, state so.

Section 1 — Macro data releases from the prior calendar month
Per indicator: latest value, release date, prior release, trailing 3-month trend.
- CPI headline and core (YoY, MoM)
- PPI headline (YoY, MoM)
- Non-farm payrolls (latest, 3-month average, revisions)
- Unemployment rate (U-3)
- Retail sales (monthly change, ex-autos if relevant)
- GDP growth rate (if released; advance vs. prior estimate)

Section 2 — Federal Reserve and FOMC developments
- FOMC meeting: decision, statement text changes vs. previous, dot plot updates, press conference key points
- Fed speeches with market-moving content: speaker, date, venue, key quotes, observable reaction
- Fed funds futures implied path vs. most recent dot plot

Section 3 — Earnings aggregate status (S&P 500)
- If active season: % reported, aggregate EPS beat rate, sales beat rate, EPS surprise magnitude
- Change in forward 12-month S&P 500 EPS consensus over the prior month
- Sector-level aggregate divergences

Section 4 — Geopolitical events of material consequence
Global trade, oil/commodities, sovereign credit, or global risk sentiment. Per event: what happened, source, observable market reaction.

Section 5 — Policy environment
- Regulatory changes affecting broad sectors: agency, rule, effective date
- Tariff and trade developments
- Major legislation: bill name, status, market-relevant provisions

Section 6 — Cross-asset and risk-sentiment indicators (compensatory)
- VIX level and trailing trend
- Credit spreads (IG and HY OAS)
- USD index trend
- 10Y yield trend, yield curve shape

Close PART 1 with a 3–5 sentence summary of the month's character — strategy-blind language only.

OUTPUT 2 — **write the 5-axis regime scores to `events.regime_events` (scope `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS`)**: one row per axis (growth_momentum / inflation_trend / policy_stance / risk_sentiment / shock_overlay) + the `_integrative` row, each with its categorical value + brief rationale (+ a `fallback_suppression` flag row when applicable). **Score ONLY the most-recently-completed covered month here — never one row per covered month.** M1b/the router read only the LATEST `events.regime_events` row, so on a multi-month catch-up the earlier missed month(s) surfaced in PART 1 are backward context/trend color only; this OUTPUT 2 5-axis score stays a single current snapshot, exactly as today. The `Monthly_Fundamental_RegimeScore.md` file is RETIRED 2026-06-06 (Operating_Protocols §15) — do NOT recreate it. This is M1b's sole regime input from M1a, which M1b reads from `state.current_regime` / `events.regime_events`:

First line: YYYY-MM marker.
Second line: fallback_suppression flag (true / false). If ≥2 of the 5 primary input categories (macro / Fed / earnings / geopolitical / policy — input 6 is compensatory and does not count) were unavailable per the fallback protocol, set true.

If fallback_suppression = true: write only the suppression rationale and exit. Do not score axes.

If fallback_suppression = false: score the 5 regime condition axes per Strategy.md's M1a template. Per axis: assigned value, brief rationale (max 3 sentences) citing which inputs drove the call. NO references to strategies, strategy letters, or per-strategy mechanisms. The 5 axes (per Strategy.md):
- growth_momentum: { accelerating | stable | decelerating }
- inflation_trend: { disinflating | stable | reaccelerating }
- policy_stance: { dovish | neutral | hawkish }
- risk_sentiment: { risk-on | neutral | stressed }
- shock_overlay: { none | latent | acute }

**`shock_overlay` IS GRADED AGAINST A WRITTEN RUBRIC, NOT ON JUDGMENT ALONE (added 2026-09-05, Rev 48).** Score that axis per Strategy.md `## Regime scoring (strategy-blind, monthly)` → `### Shock / overlay grading rubric` (generated slice `strategy/09`), which fixes what counts as a qualifying shock event, the pre-shock Brent baseline and the shock elevation measured off it, the entry condition for each of the three tokens above, and — the piece the axis previously lacked entirely — a REQUIRED `acute` → `latent` de-escalation test: downgrade once BOTH legs hold, zero new qualifying events for 15 consecutive trading days AND a Brent retracement of at least 50% of the shock elevation; either leg failing keeps the grade at `acute`. Escalation stays immediate on any qualifying event with active transmission, and that asymmetry is deliberate. The rubric's RATIONALE-RECORDING DUTY binds this OUTPUT: `shock_overlay`'s rationale must state (1) the date of the most recent qualifying event, (2) the pre-shock baseline / peak / current Brent triplet with the observation count the baseline was computed over, and (3) which transmission legs held and which failed — so every monthly score leaves a dated, measured anchor for the next scoring, the re-risking limb's leg (b), and any out-of-cycle re-score (M1R) to move off, rather than a bare verdict. The rubric CONSTRAINS judgment, it does not replace it: a score that departs from its anchors must argue against them, by name, in the same rationale.

Followed by a 2–3 sentence integrative summary of the regime in strategy-blind terms (e.g., "decelerating growth + hawkish policy + neutral risk sentiment, no acute shock") — do not name strategies.

CHAT OUTPUT: one-line acknowledgment naming both files written. If fallback_suppression = true, additionally state "FALLBACK SUPPRESSION ACTIVE — M1b will not produce strategy mappings this month."

**`ops.web_calls` OBLIGATION (added 2026-08-24, fleet-wide alert-triage closure)** — M1a's own metered surface is narrow but real: the OUTPUT 1 macro-indicators ingest calls `mcp__FMP__economics` (`treasury-rates` + `economics-indicators`, including the date-pinned `treasury_10y`/`treasury_2y` reads under the five-metrics rule above), and the `hy_oas` pull (plus the optional `yield_curve_10y2y` cross-check) against `fred.stlouisfed.org` routes through Tavily extract rather than a direct fetch, per the 403 note above. Before the terminal `sp_routine_end` call, write the batched `ops.web_calls` INSERT per the shared Run-logging template (§Observability, ~line 204-227) covering every FMP `economics` call and every Tavily extract call this run actually made — including a `fallback_suppression=true` month, where the macro ingest still runs even though axis scoring is skipped. This is restated here, as at OPS1 (~line 2380-2397), because measured fleet compliance with the shared template's `ops.web_calls` clause stays low when the obligation is left only in the distant Observability section.

```
## M3. D Position Deep-Dive — deep research

```
**SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16 — see the shared Observability section's generalized guard)** — FIRST, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='M3' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed'`; if `>= 1`, output "M3 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or M3's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the deep-dive, do NOT re-overwrite `Monthly_D_Position_Deep_Dive.md`, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row.

Read access scope: Monthly cadence. May query all of `events.decision_log` (no live/archive split, §15). Open D positions' entry records are queryable in `events.decision_log` / `events.position_events`; deep-history queries are needed only if a multi-month-old context cross-reference is required.

**LONG-HORIZON SCOPE IS ROSTER-DERIVED (2026-07-18 audit — the symmetric fix to D1/W3's `reactive` generalization, closing sisa-graduate-no-signal-path for the OTHER cadence class):** this routine covers every roster-active strategy with `review_cadence: long_horizon` in `strategy/roster.yaml` — currently exactly D, so today's behavior is unchanged; a future SISA `long_horizon` graduate is picked up automatically once SL5 registers it, with no edit to this routine. For each such strategy read its own strategy slice (per the "Strategy reading" table) in place of the fixed "Strategy D section" wording below; wherever this section says "Strategy D", read "each long_horizon roster strategy". Multiple strategies write into the SAME output file as separate `## Strategy <code>` sections (the filename stays `Monthly_D_Position_Deep_Dive.md` for continuity with M4's read and the archives — historical name, roster-wide content).

Read Strategy.md (Strategy D section), Experiment_Parameters.md, Operating_Protocols.md (positions from `state.current_positions`, decisions from `events.decision_log`).

For each currently-open Strategy D position, produce thesis-status research. Write the complete content directly to `Monthly_D_Position_Deep_Dive.md` (overwrite; first line = current month in YYYY-MM format).

Per position, cover:

1. Current thesis status. Original multi-year structural thesis from entry record. Does it still hold after developments since M3's last successful completion (normally the prior month; if one or more monthly cycles were missed, cover the full span back to and including every missed month — state the actual span covered, e.g. "2026-05 through 2026-07", rather than silently treating only the immediately-prior month)?

2. Multi-year driver check. For each original thesis driver (product cycle phase, regulatory process stage, management strategic plan, thematic participation mechanism — whichever applied), has observable progress been made? Stalled? Reversed?

3. Fundamental developments. Material filings, earnings transcripts, analyst days, regulatory events, management changes, competitive moves since M3's last successful completion (normally the prior month; if one or more monthly cycles were missed, cover the full span back to and including every missed month — state the actual span covered, e.g. "2026-05 through 2026-07").

4. Invalidation criteria check. For each at-entry-defined invalidation criterion, has any been triggered?

5. Sector and theme context. Structural shifts in the secular theme or regulatory environment affecting the multi-year case.

6. Long-term tax treatment. Time to 12-month LTCG qualification; any thesis-completion signals suggesting LTCG timing coordination.

Per position: explicit recommendation (hold / close on thesis completion / close on thesis invalidation / further research). The downstream M4 routine reads these recommendations and stages exits for "close" calls and schedules research-deferral events for "further research" calls, so each recommendation must cite the specific invalidation criterion (for close calls) or the specific information gap (for further research calls).

If any position shows material thesis invalidation, set an "IMMEDIATE-ACTION" flag at the top of the file content so M4's read picks it up first.

OUTPUT: write the complete content directly to `Monthly_D_Position_Deep_Dive.md`. First line is the YYYY-MM marker. Chat output: one-line acknowledgment, plus the IMMEDIATE-ACTION flag (if any); the flag is consumed autonomously by M4's read, and on a material thesis-invalidation flag also `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','M3','immediate_action_flagged','<ticker(s) + one-line reason>','<JSON>')` so it reaches the monitored channel rather than unmonitored chat (rev 2026-07-10 — round-2 conversion; severity bumped info→warning 2026-07-16, consumption-closure CC-7 — `info` is filtered by both `alert_emailer.gs` and `alert_relay.py`, so this alert never actually reached any monitored channel until now).

**`ops.web_calls` OBLIGATION (added 2026-08-24, fleet-wide alert-triage closure)** — the per-position research required above (item 1's thesis-status-vs-developments check, item 3's fundamental-developments sweep — material filings, earnings transcripts, analyst days, regulatory events, management changes, competitive moves — and item 5's sector/theme context check) is deep research and routinely draws on Tavily search/extract and/or FMP `news`/`secFilings` calls, run per currently-open position. Unlike OPS1's single fixed `^VIX` chart probe (~line 2380-2397), M3 makes no one named call — the actual tool/endpoint set varies with how many positions are open and what each needs — so the absence of a fixed field-value example here is not license to skip the log. Before the terminal `sp_routine_end` call, write the batched `ops.web_calls` INSERT per the shared Run-logging template (§Observability, ~line 204-227), covering every Tavily/FMP/web_search/web_fetch/HF call this run actually made across every position researched.
