Every other value ever written to this field, across every prior SL2/AR_orc batch, is a full 40-char SHA, so this was one data-entry error rather than a code defect — but nothing mechanical catches it: `events.queue_events.payload` is free-form JSON with no schema validation, unlike `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review`'s `p_source_commit_sha`, which hard-ASSERTs `^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$` (`bigquery/146_adversarial_review_writer_serialization.sql`:76-78 — filename and range corrected 2026-09-09; `145_` is `adversarial_review_storage_cutover.sql`, which carries the same ASSERT at its own :74-76) and would have rejected the same literal outright. **It cost nothing that cycle only because AR_orc's Step 1.5 artifact-version gate reads the ATTACKER TRANSCRIPT's ASSERT-validated `source_commit_sha`, never this payload field — keep it that way.** This field is provenance/audit trail, never a gate input. Do not confuse it with the sibling `payload.git_commit`, which by established convention carries the SHORT hash; the two are not interchangeable, which is precisely why Step 1.5 warns that comparing a short SHA against a full one is a guaranteed false mismatch. **WRITE-SITE VERIFICATION — MANDATORY, added 2026-08-18 by SL2, the routine that owns this write.** The pin above states the CONTRACT but specifies no check, and the contract alone is exactly what already failed: `d66da712` is not a truncation of `d66da71085fb2617366a99bedd1b30bce6b04706` — its eighth character differs — so the value was hand-typed from a glance at a short hash rather than shortened from a correct one, and re-reading the same prose would not have caught it. So CAPTURE the command's output into the payload instead of transcribing a hash read off a log line or a commit summary, and VERIFY before the INSERT: the value must be 40 lowercase hex characters AND `git cat-file -t <sha>` must return `commit`. One local git call, no network, no BigQuery cost. It is the ONLY guard this field has — `events.queue_events.payload` is unvalidated free-form JSON, so unlike `ops.sp_write_adversarial_review`'s `p_source_commit_sha` regex ASSERT there is no write-time rejection anywhere downstream, and a bad value that lands is durable. A detector view over already-landed payloads was considered here and deliberately NOT built: this is the field's only origination site, so a guard AT the writer prevents the class outright where a detector could only report it after the fact, and adding live SQL for it would multiply machinery for a field that by the pin above is provenance-only and gates nothing. **THE 2026-08-17 VALUES WERE ALREADY REPAIRED IN BAND — do NOT write a correction row for them.** Read the pin above as history, not as a live defect. AR_att's 2026-08-18 fire consumed both `pending` rows and carried the field forward CORRECTED on its own `attacker-complete` rows — `premortem-C-2026-a3` cycle 14 (`event_id` `6c8b2386-b8bd-40b2-8a00-690b9d5b8253`) and `premortem-E-2026-a3` cycle 10 (`event_id` `a0ca0390-ffbf-4f15-a690-bb047fac5a0b`), each carrying `artifact_source_commit='d66da71085fb2617366a99bedd1b30bce6b04706'` plus a `payload.enqueue_payload_commit_note` recording what the consumed row had said and why it was wrong. Because `state.open_queue_detail` is latest-`event_ts`-wins, the live payload for both items is ALREADY correct and the malformed string survives only on the superseded row — which is what append-only history is FOR. SL2's own `due_date_correction` precedent (2026-08-17) does not transfer to this field and must not be copied onto it: that correction was written while the rows were SL2's own un-consumed `PENDING_DRAFT` items, whereas these sit mid-cycle in the AR_att→AR_orc handoff with `orchestrator_due_date` one day out, and a fresh SL2 row on top of them would move each item's latest `event_id` and `event_ts` underneath the very `open_queue_detail`-to-`adversarial_reviews_current` join AR_orc's STEP 0 uses to detect a stranded verdict — buying nothing, since the field is provenance-only and is already right. This is the designated route for stale-sizing-mitigation revisions: replace the retired flat-2% / hard-envelope mitigation with the current no-ceiling thesis-scaled CaR discipline—the seven-factor decision-log justification plus the mandatory adversarial attack on size—preserve the historical finding, and do NOT alter entry/exit rules, thresholds, indicators, router, kill criteria, or any other strategy machinery. Any broader live-strategy defect remains terminate-and-restart-as-new; never use this route as an in-life strategy edit. The five existing `revise-premortem-<A-E>-2026-a3` tasks meet this route exactly; their historical `payload.scope_gap` and `conservative_default='NO-EDIT'` record why they were parked, not a continuing block after this correction. Beyond cycle 5, honor the rev-15 soft cap: either record the written continuation justification (the forcing-question discipline) in `events.decision_log` or abandon → write a REJECTED lifecycle row + cooldown stamp. If a redraft changes or adds a Tier 1/2/3 flag, `INSERT` its own new `events.premortem_flags` row per (A) step 2b — append-only, never edit a prior flag row in place, so the original flag_text stays available for `adversarial_flag_hit` scoring even if the strategy's final accepted mechanism moved past it.

This is the precondition SL1 enforces before any restart. **SCORE PRE-MORTEM FLAGS (self-improvement audit ITEM 22, 2026-07-11).** Read every `events.premortem_flags` row for this `strategy_code`. For each, read its `review_trigger_text` and — from the strategy's real trade/decision history (`events.decision_log`, `perf.strategy_daily`, `events.regime_events`) plus the post-mortem's own `what_revealed`/`what_unresolved` you just authored — make ONE judgment: did that flag's named review-trigger condition actually occur before the loss/termination event (`trigger_fired = TRUE`), and if so did it occur BEFORE the loss became visible in the numbers (`fired_before_loss`) or only in hindsight? `INSERT INTO events.premortem_flag_outcomes` (`flag_id`, `trigger_fired`, `fired_before_loss`, `evidence_text` — a one-to-two-sentence citation of what you read, `judge_session` = this run's session context). A flag whose trigger never fired is scored `trigger_fired = FALSE`, not skipped — the whole point of `analytics.adversarial_flag_hit` is measuring the pre-mortem's catch rate, which needs the misses recorded as honestly as the hits.

**THE PRE-MORTEM'S `**Revision:** N` MARKER IS AN INDEPENDENT COUNTER OVER THE ARTIFACT TEXT — NEVER DERIVED FROM `cycle_number` (PINNED 2026-08-20, before its first divergent write).** Routes (A) and (B) both write that marker and neither says a word about how its value is chosen. A repo-wide search establishes the negative: **no document anywhere states the rule** — not this file, not `task_plan/SL2.md`/`AR_att.md`/`AR_orc.md`, not `Experiment_Parameters.md`'s pre-mortem-format section, not `Operating_Protocols.md`, not `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md`'s own preamble, not `strategy/roster.yaml` — and **nothing mechanical guards it**: no script, CI check, dbt test or SQL object parses or asserts on the literal `**Revision:**` string (`scripts/check_roster_consistency.py` segments this very file per strategy and never looks at it), while the artifact-version machinery keys on the **SHA256 of the section text** and `cycle_number` keys on `events.adversarial_reviews`. The marker is therefore unguarded free text that only a routine's own discipline keeps correct — the same standing as `payload.artifact_source_commit` above, and it earns the same write-site rule.

The reason it was never written down is that until recently the question had no content: rev and cycle were the same integer on **every** revision SL2 has ever written, and SL2's own record says both in one breath at every site — `events.decision_log` "Revised to rev 9 … re-enqueued for cycle 9" (D; B at 11, C at 13, E at 9, all 2026-08-13), "Revised to rev 10 … cycle 10" (E) and "rev 14 … cycle 14" (C, 2026-08-17), and `ops.alerts` "C rev 14 (cycle 14), E rev 10 (cycle 10)". Nothing in that record distinguishes a counter that TRACKS the cycle from one that merely happened to equal it. **Three mechanisms break the identity, in both directions:**

- **Revision advances, no cycle at all — and this already happened, in April.** The **router** pre-mortem's own text reads "**Revision:** 5 (2026-04-23) … Rev 5 applies a spot-edit fix to those 2 items under the revision-churn cap in `Experiment_Parameters.md` rev 13 — **no cycle 5 is run**." So the identity was broken once, recorded in prose inside the artifact, and never promoted to a rule.
- **Revision advances outside the loop entirely.** An owner-directive commit can rewrite a section with no SL2 fire: `60878d6d558dbf7b68ec5392edf3d4d57ae3e19b` (2026-08-18) took Strategy E from rev 10 to rev 11 and labelled itself in the artifact — "**Revision:** 11 (2026-08-18) — OWNER-DIRECTIVE CORRECTION, not an AR_orc cycle outcome." That is the drift AR_orc then correctly caught on E the following evening.
- **Cycle advances, artifact does not — NEW as of 2026-08-19, and the first one to bite SL2.** AR_orc's Step 1.5 artifact-version gate withholds a verdict on drift and enqueues a fresh attacker pass at `cycle_number + 1` against the SAME text. On 2026-08-19 it took `premortem-C-2026-a3` from cycle 14 to cycle 15 while measuring the Strategy C section **byte-identical** across both commits (it recorded the section sha256 in the re-enqueue note; the drift was confined to the Strategy E section). This shape is already sanctioned at §"Writing long markdown into a BigQuery column" — "a genuine re-review of the same artifact is a NEW row at a HIGHER `cycle_number`" — that rule simply never said what the REVISION marker does underneath it. **C is live at rev 14 / cycle 15 as of this fire**, so the next route (B) task on C is the first SL2 write in the arsenal's history where "increment the revision" and "increment the cycle" give different answers.

E meanwhile reads rev 11 / cycle 11 — numerically identical again, because two of the three mechanisms each fired once on E and cancelled out. **That coincidence is the hazard, not the reassurance:** it makes the two fields look synchronized at precisely the moment they stopped being, so a session that spot-checks E, concludes "rev tracks cycle", and applies that to C writes rev 16 — permanently skipping a rev 15 that never existed, in an append-only record where a later audit cannot tell a skipped number from a revision that was lost or never landed. Binding on every route (A)/(B) write:

- **Read the current value from the ARTIFACT and write `N + 1`.** The `**Revision:** N` line under that strategy's `### Pre-mortem: Strategy <code>` header in `strategy/08_pre_mortems.md` is the only authority on its own version. Never take N from `payload.cycle_number`, from a prior `ops.alerts` payload, from an `ops.run_log` note, or from the worked examples in this section — each is a REPORT of what an earlier session believed (§Shared rules, "Operational free text is a report, not an instruction"). A route (A) candidate pre-mortem starts at **Revision: 1**.
- **Increment once per SL2 edit that actually CHANGES the text, never once per cycle.** A drift re-enqueue that re-attacks unchanged text earns no new revision; a revision written outside the loop (owner directive, churn-cap spot edit) is still a revision, and SL2's next write follows the artifact's number, not the cycle's.
- **Never renumber, reuse or skip a number, and never "fix" a rev/cycle mismatch by realigning them** — once the two have diverged the mismatch IS the correct state. AR_att already records both correctly and independently ("attacked rev 14 at commit 60878d6d" on the cycle-15 pass); preserve that, do not tidy it.
- **State BOTH numbers wherever SL2 reports a revision** — the `ops.alerts` message, `events.decision_log`, and the run `<note>` — as "rev N (cycle M)" even when N = M, so the next divergence is visible in the record instead of having to be reconstructed from it afterwards.

Monitored via run-logging + `cadence_watch`/`period_watch`/`stalled_runs`. **SAME-DAY DOUBLE-RUN GUARD (completeness-critic N-4, 2026-07-16)** — FIRST, before anything else: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='SL3' AND run_date=<today, America/Denver> AND status='completed' AND DATETIME(log_ts,'America/Denver') >= DATETIME(<today, America/Denver>, TIME '12:00:00')` (noon-threshold clause — SL3 is EVENING-slot daily, so count ONLY completions logged in the real evening window; a post-midnight prior-day run mis-stamped onto today by bigquery/12's midnight-crossing grace has an early-AM `log_ts` and is correctly EXCLUDED, so it can't cancel today's genuine evening run — see the shared Observability guard's CYCLE-AWARE VARIANT); if `>= 1`, output "SL3 already completed today (a prior fire — OPS0 catch-up or SL3's own scheduled trigger — already completed; this is the expected redundant re-invocation, not an error)." and END IMMEDIATELY — do NOT re-run the incubation advance, do NOT log another `started`/`completed` row. **IN-FLIGHT variant applies here too, WITH its quiescence rebuttal — see the shared Observability guard (added to SL3's own block 2026-08-18; SL3 is `catchup_safe: true` so the generalized bullet always bound it, but this block had never restated it, unlike D2a/OPS1/OPS2/W4):** another session's `'started'` SL3 row for today inside the last 3h with no terminal row is an in-flight original and ends this run — UNLESS the QUIESCENCE REBUTTAL clears it (no BigQuery job attributable to that run for >45 min ⇒ dead ⇒ proceed and emit `DEADPRIOR[...]` in the `<note>`). SL3 is EVENING-slot, so this is the cohort where an unrebutted proxy costs the whole day; the 2026-08-18 run is the worked instance.

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL3')` before the dependency gate.** RAISEs + `critical` alert (abort) if the arsenal loop is disabled/frozen. (Incubation itself does NOT gate on `ops.trading_control` — only the eventual PROBE launch does, see STEP 3.)

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('SL3', ['D2a'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log.** Aborts (RAISE) + `missing_dependency` critical if D2a has not logged `completed` for today (SL3 measures against D2a's freshly-ingested marks). Self-bootstrapping.

STEP 1 — UPDATE THE FORWARD-TEST SERIES. **Catch-up loop (owner directive 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW — see Observability § above): for EVERY missed trading day between SL3's own last successful completion (`state.routine_catchup_window` for routine='SL3', or `SELECT MAX(run_date) FROM ops.run_log WHERE routine='SL3' AND status='completed'` as fallback) and today's `last_trading_day` that has a `state.daily_marks_curated` row — oldest first — run the SHADOW/PAPER bullets below against THAT day's marks, not only today's (this backfill depends on D2a's own marks catch-up — see D2a — a day D2a never marked cannot be evaluated here).** For every SHADOW/PAPER strategy in `state.strategy_roster`:
   - SHADOW: compute router activation + entry/exit SIGNALS against fresh `events.daily_marks` (zero orders, zero capital); record would-be-trade regime cell + signal-generation rate vs declared frequency + scaffolding correctness to `analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` (`phase='shadow'`) and record each would-be signal as an `events.shadow_positions` row (`event_type='SIGNAL'`, `is_paper=TRUE`, `regime_cell`, `note` = one-line signal rationale). The `regime_cell` value MUST use the two-token coverage key `SPY_TREND/VIX_REGIME` (for example `NEUTRAL/NORMAL`), with both tokens drawn from `strategy/01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md`; yield-curve and breadth remain separate signal context. This is the exact key used by `state.arsenal_regime_coverage`.
   - PAPER: compute SIMULATED fills at live marks with modeled IBKR commissions + conservative slippage vs SGOV; update `analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` (`phase='paper'`: sim_twr, sgov_twr, excess, peak_to_trough, sim_closed_trades, per-regime-cell attribution) and record each simulated fill as `events.shadow_positions` rows (`event_type='OPEN'`/`'CLOSE'`, `shares`/`price`/`commission` = the modeled values, `is_paper=TRUE`). Zero real orders — `events.shadow_positions` (is_paper=TRUE) is excluded from every live capital/kill view. IDEMPOTENCY GUARD (required — OPS0 catchup autofire can re-invoke SL3 same-day, and now also a genuine multi-day catch-up loop covering more than one trading day in one session): before each insert, NOT-EXISTS check on (strategy_code, event_type, ticker, DATE(event_ts) = <the trading day currently being processed, today included>) — skip already-recorded rows, mirroring the `ops.roster_change_log` NOT-EXISTS pattern.
   - **`analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` WRITE CONTRACT — PINNED (SL3 2026-08-19 diligence sweep, handoff-wiring class); binds BOTH bullets above.** That table has exactly three `NOT NULL`-with-no-default columns — `strategy_code`, `phase`, and **`incubation_day` (DATE)** — and until this line, `incubation_day` appeared **nowhere in this document at all**, while SL3 is its ONLY writer. Same shape as the SL3→SL5 `PENDING_ROSTER` lane (fixed 6467b4d) and the SL5 `change_key` strings (pinned 2026-08-19): a required column the write site's own text never names. Two things are pinned, and the second matters more than the first:
     - **`incubation_day` = the trading day currently being processed by the catch-up loop above — NEVER `CURRENT_DATE()`.** Every gate in STEP 2 is computed off it and a session that stamped today's date onto a backfilled day would corrupt all of them silently: `shadow_days` and `paper_days` are `COUNT(DISTINCT incubation_day)` (`bigquery/60`:34; `bigquery/35`'s `paper_days` alias), so a multi-day catch-up run would collapse N days into ONE and push the 20-day SHADOW and 60-day PAPER floors permanently out of reach; and `excess_met` reads `ARRAY_AGG(excess ORDER BY incubation_day DESC LIMIT 10)` (`bigquery/35`'s `trailing_excess` CTE, read by its `excess_met` alias), so a wrong stamp reorders the trailing-10-day sustained-excess window at the highest-stakes PAPER→PROBE gate. It is also the table's `PARTITION BY` key (`bigquery/35`'s `PARTITION BY incubation_day CLUSTER BY strategy_code, phase` clause), so a `CURRENT_DATE()` stamp mis-partitions the row as well as mis-dating it. The full column set: `strategy_code`, `phase` (`'shadow'`/`'paper'`), `incubation_day`, plus the phase's own measures (`signals_generated`/`scaffolding_faults` for shadow; `sim_twr`/`sgov_twr`/`excess`/`peak_to_trough`/`sim_closed_trades` for paper) and `regime_cell`; `computed_ts` defaults.
     - **CITATION FORM — audited 2026-08-23, do NOT re-add a `:NNN` pin into `bigquery/35`.** All 19 `path:NNN` citations in this section were resolved against the tree: 12 accurate, 6 drifted, 1 (the `bigquery/133` F/G claim, corrected in STEP 4) an overclaim rather than a stale number. **Every drift was in `bigquery/35_strategy_arsenal.sql` — 6 of its 7 pins — because that file keeps accreting long inline notes above the constructs cited here**, while the pins into `bigquery/52`, `bigquery/60` and `bigquery/01_schema.sql` were accurate without exception. The `bigquery/35` citations are therefore now named anchors (`paper_days` alias, the `trailing_excess` column alias inside the `agg` CTE, the `PARTITION BY` clause, `not_already_transitioned`, the `cooldown_until DATE` column, the `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`/`CREATE TABLE` statements) — **two of those six sharpened 2026-08-24 (SL3) after a re-audit resolved every anchor against the tree: `trailing_excess` is a column alias, NOT a CTE of its own (it lives inside the `agg` CTE), and `not_already_transitioned` is the ONE anchor here that is not self-disambiguating — a bare grep for it hits THREE different readiness views in `bigquery/35` (the `UNDER_REVIEW->SHADOW` adoption one, the `SHADOW->PAPER` shadow one, and the `PAPER->PROBE` paper one), so always grep it together with the `change_key` literal named alongside it in the prose, never by the alias name alone.** An anchor that resolves to three places is the same hazard as a drifted line number in a slower form, all grep-resolvable; the pins into the three stable files are left as measured-correct line numbers rather than churned. **A drifted pin is worse than no pin — it points at real code that is not the code meant.**
     - **THE IDEMPOTENCY GUARD ABOVE MUST COVER THIS TABLE TOO — NOT-EXISTS on `(strategy_code, phase, incubation_day)` before each insert.** As written, that guard named only `events.shadow_positions`, leaving the perf table with no re-run protection even though the same two re-invocation paths (an OPS0 catch-up autofire, and the multi-day catch-up loop) hit both. This is NOT harmless duplication that the DISTINCT day-counts absorb: `state.strategy_shadow_readiness` **SUMs** `signals_generated` and `scaffolding_faults` across rows (`bigquery/60`:35-36), and since `bigquery/52_shadow_readiness_band.sql` gave `signal_rate_ok` an archetype-aware upper CEILING rather than a bare floor (`bigquery/52`:69, live at `bigquery/60`:64), a duplicated day inflates the signal count toward that ceiling — so a re-run can push a genuinely healthy candidate to `signal_rate_ok=FALSE`, and, once `shadow_days >= 400`, straight into STEP 4's SHADOW time-cull as `stuck`. The failure direction is a **false REJECT of a sound candidate**, which no other rail catches.
   - **`events.shadow_positions` WRITE CONTRACT — `event_ts` MUST BE STAMPED TO THE TRADING DAY BEING PROCESSED, NEVER LEFT TO DEFAULT (SL3 2026-08-26 diligence sweep; the sibling half of the `incubation_day` pin above, left open when that one was closed).** `events.shadow_positions` has exactly one `NOT NULL`-with-no-default column (`strategy_code`), so the required-column audit that produced the pin above comes back clean here — and that is precisely why this defect survived it. The exposure is not a missing required column; it is a **defaulted** one whose default is wrong for this writer. `event_ts` is `TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()` and is also the table's partition key (`bigquery/35_strategy_arsenal.sql`'s `CREATE TABLE … events.shadow_positions` block and its `PARTITION BY DATE(event_ts) CLUSTER BY strategy_code` clause), while SL3's block names `event_ts` exactly twice — at STEP 3 and STEP 4, both times to say it defaults, and both times about `events.strategy_lifecycle`, where defaulting is CORRECT because a lifecycle transition genuinely happens at write time. **A `shadow_positions` row does not: it records a signal or a simulated fill that happened on a specific trading day, which during a catch-up backfill is NOT today.** Neither STEP 1 bullet tells the session to supply `event_ts`, so as written every backfilled row lands stamped with the RUN date.
     - **This silently defeats STEP 1's own idempotency guard, in BOTH directions.** The guard keys on `DATE(event_ts) = <the trading day currently being processed>` — a column that, unstamped, carries the run date instead. So (a) for every backfilled day X ≠ today the guard is **vacuous**: no row ever carries `DATE(event_ts) = X`, so a second session covering the same catch-up window re-inserts every one of them — the exact re-run exposure the guard exists to close; and (b) worse, within a SINGLE multi-day catch-up session processing oldest-first, every row already written for days X₁…Xₙ₋₁ carries `DATE(event_ts) = today`, so when the loop reaches today the guard's NOT-EXISTS **matches those backfill rows** for any coinciding `(strategy_code, event_type, ticker)` and **skips today's genuine signal as "already recorded"**. A systematic strategy re-firing on the same ticker across consecutive days is the NORMAL case, not an exotic one, so that collision is likely rather than remote. Direction (b) is a silent LOSS of live signal evidence, which is strictly worse than the duplication in (a) and is the same failure direction — a false negative on the candidate's own record — that the `incubation_day` pin above calls out as the one no other rail catches.
     - **Mis-partitioning is the third harm**, identical to the one the pin above states for `analytics.strategy_incubation_perf`: `PARTITION BY DATE(event_ts)` files a backfilled day's rows in today's partition. **Stamp `event_ts` explicitly on every `shadow_positions` insert** — the same trading day the loop is processing and the same value used for that row's `incubation_day`; the two tables are written from one loop iteration and must agree on what day it is. `events.shadow_positions` holds **0 rows** (verified live 2026-08-26), so — like the `SHADOW->PAPER` marker (2026-08-19) and the `->REJECTED` marker (2026-08-20) — this is closed before its first firing with no historical row to remap. SL3 is the table's only writer anywhere in the repo (repo-wide grep, 2026-08-26: `bigquery/35`'s DDL, `ops/handoff_contracts.yaml`'s registration of it as SL3's write surface, `ops/cadence.yaml`'s scope list, and SL3's own text — no other write site), so no other routine's text needs the same pin.
   - **`regime_cell` MUST BE RESOLVED AS-OF THE TRADING DAY BEING PROCESSED, AND ITS SOURCE IS `events.regime_events` — NOT `state.current_regime` (SL3 2026-08-27 diligence sweep; measured live, not inferred).** This is the THIRD as-of-dated field in these same two write sites and the last one still unpinned. The two already closed have the identical shape — a per-day value that a catch-up backfill silently fills with the RUN day's value: `incubation_day` (2026-08-19) and `events.shadow_positions.event_ts` (2026-08-26, the bullet directly above). `regime_cell` was never pinned because the STEP 1 SHADOW bullet pins its FORMAT and stops there: it requires the two-token `SPY_TREND/VIX_REGIME` key with both tokens drawn from `strategy/01_shared_regime_vocabulary.md`, and says nothing whatever about the field's SOURCE or its AS-OF DATE. **This section names `regime_cell` four times and `state.arsenal_regime_coverage` five, and names no source object for it even once**; the Read access scope line above granted none either (corrected in this same revision).
     - **The source is `events.regime_events`, read at `as_of_date = <the trading day currently being processed>`.** D2a — SL3's own declared dependency, so the dependency gate already guarantees the row is written before SL3 runs — writes one `scope='TECHNICAL_SIGNAL'` row per trading day for each of `key='SPY_TREND'` and `key='VIX_REGIME'`, carrying `as_of_date` and the exact vocabulary tokens, into a table that is `PARTITION BY as_of_date CLUSTER BY scope, key` (`bigquery/01_schema.sql`'s `CREATE TABLE … events.regime_events` block). Compose the cell as `CONCAT(<SPY_TREND value>, '/', <VIX_REGIME value>)` — which is exactly the key `state.arsenal_regime_coverage`'s own `cells` CTE builds by `CROSS JOIN`ing `['UP','NEUTRAL','DOWN']` against `['LOW','NORMAL','HIGH']`. Where a day carries more than one row for a key, take the latest by `(event_ts DESC, event_id DESC)` — the same tiebreaker `state.current_regime`'s `QUALIFY` uses, and for the reason its own inline comment gives (two events can share `(as_of_date, event_ts)` for one `(scope, key)`, as STRATEGY_ACTIVATION C did on 2026-06-03, so without the `event_id` term the resolved cell can flip between query runs).
     - **Do NOT reach for `state.current_regime`, which is the trap this pin exists to close.** It is the obvious object — it is the only `state` object with "regime" in its name that carries a cell at all, and `state.arsenal_regime_coverage` is the coverage GRID rather than a daily series — but its body is `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY scope, key ORDER BY as_of_date DESC, event_ts DESC, event_id DESC) = 1` (`bigquery/01_schema.sql`'s `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW … state.current_regime` statement). It partitions on `(scope, key)` ONLY and returns exactly one row per key — the latest-dated one. **It has no as-of parameter and cannot be given one**, so a backfill that reads it stamps TODAY's regime onto every day it processes, silently and with no error.
     - **Live and measured, not a theoretical hazard — the cell genuinely moves day to day.** `VIX_REGIME` read `NORMAL` on 2026-08-25 and 2026-08-26 and flipped to `LOW` on 2026-08-27 (close 14.51 < 15), and did the same a week earlier: `LOW` on 08-19 sandwiched between `NORMAL` on 08-18 and 08-20. So on the very run that wrote this pin, a backfill of 2026-08-26 reading `state.current_regime` would have stamped `UP/LOW` onto a day that was `UP/NORMAL`. All nine trading days 2026-08-17..08-27 carry a complete `SPY_TREND`/`VIX_REGIME` pair with no duplicates (verified live 2026-08-27), so a wrong cell would be a choice of the wrong OBJECT, never missing data.
     - **The harm is worse than a mis-dated row, and it lands at the gate that spends money.** `regime_cell` is the column `state.arsenal_regime_coverage`'s `demonstrated` CTE groups by (`GROUP BY p.strategy_code, p.regime_cell` over `phase='paper'` rows), so a wrong cell both manufactures coverage evidence in a cell the candidate never traded and withholds it from the cell it did — feeding `n_positive_cells` and the `gap_fill` disjunct of `regime_met` at the PAPER→PROBE gate, the first time an autonomously-adopted strategy takes real capital. Two things make it nastier than its two closed siblings: it is the only one of the three NOT a partition key, so no mis-partitioning symptom ever surfaces to hint at it; and it can move the gate in BOTH directions, where `incubation_day` and `event_ts` fail only toward a false REJECT — a run-day cell that happens to be a fresh one raises `n_positive_cells` and can graduate a candidate on breadth it never demonstrated. Read alongside the `regime_met` vacuity pin in STEP 2 (2026-08-25): that one says the `>= 2` breadth bar cannot bind on the first graduation, and this one says the evidence feeding it can be wrong — same gate, independent defects.
     - **FALLBACK, deliberately the fail-safe one: if the processed day has no `SPY_TREND`/`VIX_REGIME` pair in `events.regime_events`, write `regime_cell = NULL`** (the column is nullable in BOTH tables STEP 1 writes it to — **`bigquery/35` carries a `regime_cell STRING` line TWICE, once inside its `CREATE TABLE … events.shadow_positions` block and once inside its `CREATE TABLE … analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` block, and neither is `NOT NULL`; disambiguated 2026-08-31 (SL3), which is why the anchor now names the enclosing block rather than the bare column line.** A bare grep for `regime_cell STRING` resolves to two different tables — the same two-places-not-one hazard the 2026-08-24 sweep sharpened `not_already_transitioned` for, and the only anchor in this block that still carried it; the underlying claim is unaffected, since the fallback is legitimate against both) and say so in the `<note>`. Do NOT substitute the run day's cell, and do NOT carry the nearest neighbouring day's forward. The coverage view already handles NULL explicitly (`WHERE p.phase = 'paper' AND p.regime_cell IS NOT NULL`), so a NULL drops the row out of the grid and UNDERSTATES breadth, whereas a substituted cell MANUFACTURES it — and manufactured breadth is precisely the failure `regime_met` exists to prevent. Understating is the SISA default-REJECT direction. The case is genuinely reachable: STEP 1's catch-up loop keys on days carrying a `state.daily_marks_curated` row, and D2a's regime write is a separate step from its marks ingest, so a day can in principle carry marks and no regime pair.
     - Closed BEFORE its first firing — `analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` and `events.shadow_positions` both hold **0 rows** (verified live 2026-08-27), so no historical row needs remapping, the same position as the `incubation_day`, `event_ts`, `SHADOW->PAPER` and `->REJECTED` pins. **Prose only: no live SQL, no view and no gate is changed by this revision**, per the same posture as the 2026-08-25 `regime_met` referral — an incubation-monitor fire hardens its own read side and does not unilaterally edit a capital-adjacent gate.

STEP 2 — EVALUATE READINESS (objective views; the PAPER view encodes the anti-churn caps — the SHADOW view deliberately encodes none, see the term-naming pin below — and each encodes a NOT-EXISTS-later-state idempotency guard against `ops.roster_change_log`).
   - `state.strategy_shadow_readiness.ready` = `days_met` AND signal rate within the declared band AND zero scaffolding faults AND `arsenal_ok` AND not-already-transitioned.
     - **THE FIRST CONJUNCT USED TO READ `>= min_shadow_trading_days`, WHICH NAMES A POLICY RECORD NOTHING READS RATHER THAN THE VIEW COLUMN IT DESCRIBES (SL3 2026-09-06 diligence sweep; measured against the live view body and `scripts/`, not inferred).** This is the residue of the same defect the 2026-09-03 sweep corrected two slots away, in a milder form: `caps_ok` and `theater_ok` were names of a DIFFERENT view, while `min_shadow_trading_days` is a name from a different LAYER. It is not a phantom — it is real at `strategy/roster.yaml`'s `rails:` block, where it reads `min_shadow_trading_days: 20` — but **nothing resolves it to anything.** The number that actually governs SHADOW graduation is a bare literal `20` compiled into the view (`COALESCE(a.shadow_days, 0) >= 20 AS days_met`, live in `bigquery/60_shadow_stuck_cull.sql` and byte-identical in `dbt/models/state/strategy_shadow_readiness.sql`), which reads no table, no config and no roster value. So the YAML entry and the SQL literal are two independent 20s that merely agree today. Corrected to `days_met`, the view's own column name, matching the other four conjuncts. The PAPER line below is left as `>= ~60 paper trading days`: its `~` was already doing the honest work of NOT claiming a parameter, and the PAPER threshold has no policy name at all to be wrong about (see the sub-bullet under it).
     - **THE UNWIRED RAIL IS NOT SL3'S TO FIX, AND IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN CARRIED SILENTLY.** `strategy/roster.yaml` declares itself authoritative for roster governance, so an owner or a later session that edited `min_shadow_trading_days: 20` to `40` believing it had tightened the SHADOW gate would change nothing and be told nothing: the key appears in NEITHER `RAIL_NAMES` nor `ROSTER_RAIL_KEY_TO_SQL_NAME` in `scripts/check_roster_consistency.py` — the two lists that cross-check every OTHER rail (`n_min`, `n_max`, `k_incubate`, `k_regime`, `max_roundtrip_commission_bps`, `adoption_rate_window_days`) against the SQL — and a repo-wide grep finds no script reading either `min_shadow_trading_days` or `shadow_days` at all. **This is a KNOWN, deliberately-undone follow-up, not a discovery**: `bigquery/52_shadow_readiness_band.sql`'s own header says so outright — it added the key to `roster.yaml` as a policy record and states that "wiring a full R-E-style CI cross-check for it … is a reasonable follow-up, not done here." It is the same SHAPE as SL3's open `roster.yaml` cull-staleness referral (the file the system calls its source of truth asserting something live state does not honour), on the same surface, with the same owner. A SQL comment is not a venue under the 2026-08-28 OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule, so it is raised this run as an `ops.alerts` `info` row (`roster_rail_declared_unenforced`) naming `strategy/roster.yaml` + `scripts/check_roster_consistency.py`. **The PAPER side is strictly worse and the same row covers it:** the `>= 60` literal has no mirror in `roster.yaml` or anywhere else — not even an unwired one — so there is no `min_paper_trading_days` to be stale, only an undeclared constant. **Do NOT add either key to `RAIL_NAMES` from an SL3 fire**: that is a CI change on landed, green history, the failure CLAUDE.md warns about by name, and SL3 edits no repo governance surface by design.
   - `state.strategy_paper_readiness.ready` = `>= ~60 paper trading days` AND `trades_met` (self-improvement audit ITEM 9, 2026-07-11 — archetype-aware: `>= 10` simulated closed trades for a fast-turnover candidate (`declared_annual_roundtrips IS NULL OR >= 10`), else `>= GREATEST(3, CEIL(declared_annual_roundtrips / 2))` for a declared slow/long-horizon archetype — so a D-like candidate is no longer structurally unable to ever graduate) AND `excess_met` (self-improvement audit ITEM 8, 2026-07-11 — sustained, not a single lucky day: cumulative paper excess-vs-SGOV `>= 0` on EACH of the trailing 10 incubation days, not just the latest) AND regime coverage (positive excess in `>=2` cells OR fills a zero-coverage arsenal cell) AND adoption-rate window open AND roster below `n_max` AND `arsenal_ok` AND not-already-transitioned.
     - **`regime_met` IS VACUOUS ON THE FIRST GRADUATION — its two disjuncts are not two tests, and the parenthetical above reads as though they are (SL3 2026-08-25 diligence sweep; measured live, not inferred).** `regime_met` (the `regime_met` alias in `bigquery/189_paper_stuck_completeness.sql`, and the identical one in `bigquery/35_strategy_arsenal.sql`) is `n_positive_cells >= 2 OR <gap_fill matched>`, where the `positive_cells` CTE counts the candidate's own distinct `regime_cell`s carrying a `phase='paper'` row with `excess >= 0`, and the `gap_fill` CTE matches the candidate if ANY such row lands in a `state.arsenal_regime_coverage` cell whose `is_gap` is TRUE. **All nine cells are `is_gap = TRUE` today and will stay that way until the first SISA-grown strategy reaches PROBE**, so the second disjunct is satisfied by a SINGLE positive-excess paper day and the whole term collapses to `n_positive_cells >= 1`. The `>= 2` breadth bar therefore cannot bind on the one decision it was written for — the FIRST PAPER→PROBE graduation, the first time an autonomously-adopted strategy takes real capital. Worse, `excess_met` already demands cumulative paper excess `>= 0` on each of the trailing 10 incubation days, so a candidate that clears `excess_met` has almost certainly already cleared the reduced `regime_met`: as it stands the term adds close to nothing to the gate. **Why all nine cells are gaps, and why it is not a defect in the view:** `is_gap` is `covered_active_count = 0` (the `cov` CTE's `COUNTIF(r.is_active AND d.positive_excess)` over the `demonstrated` CTE, which reads `analytics.strategy_incubation_perf` `phase='paper'` rows ONLY), and SL3 STEP 1 is that table's ONLY writer anywhere in the repo, writing solely for members currently in SHADOW/PAPER. So the dedup predicate can never match a prior day's row, `sp_raise_alert_once` degenerates to a plain `sp_raise_alert`, and the stall raises a NEW alert every day it persists — the precise pile-up the call was chosen to prevent, on a condition whose only remedy is an owner deposit that may legitimately take days or weeks. **Fix, and it is entirely within this line's gift: keep the varying integers OUT of the `<message>` and carry them in the payload, where they already belong.** Raise a STABLE message — `CONCAT(strategy_code, ' is frozen below the $2,000 probe floor — deposit or sunset-redistribution routing needed; the deposit is the sanctioned owner touch, this alert is the in-band surfacing bigquery/62\'s header promised but never wired')` — and put `days_since_probe_entry` / `funding_gap_dollars` / `booked_allocation` in the payload argument. This is the ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICES payload rule applied here ("the payload is enrichment and the message is not; the `<message>` argument MUST stand alone as a complete sentence"), and with a stable message the dedup works exactly as this line always claimed: one open alert per stalled strategy, not one per stalled strategy per day. **Also pin the payload's CONSTRUCTION, not just its content:** `in_payload_json` is a **`STRING`**, not BigQuery's native `JSON` type, and `sp_raise_alert` stores it via `SAFE.PARSE_JSON(in_payload_json)` — so pass `TO_JSON_STRING(<row>)` (the construction `ops.sp_log_decision`'s own body uses for this identical argument position). A literal `TO_JSON(...)` there does **not** implicitly coerce and fails to compile the `CALL` outright on the first stall; a merely malformed string is quieter and worse, since `SAFE.PARSE_JSON` does not error — it stores `payload = NULL` and the alert loses its whole context with nothing surfaced. The `<row as JSON>` shorthand this line used left both traps open — and went on leaving them open until 2026-09-08, because the 2026-08-26 pass that wrote this sentence corrected the paragraph and not the template; see the payload-argument correction recorded with the TEMPLATE ITSELF CORRECTED note above. **THAT RESIDUAL IS NOW CLOSED — AND CLOSING IT HANDED SL3 A STANDING DUTY THIS BLOCK DID NOT CARRY (corrected 2026-08-31, SL3 diligence sweep; measured live against `ops.alert_policy`, not inferred).** Until this revision the text here read that `probe_funding_stalled` "has **no row in `ops.alert_policy`** (verified live 2026-08-26 — 0 rows for that category, against 34 registered ones)", that it was therefore "LATCHING with no auto-resolve rule" so that "even after the deposit lands and the stall genuinely clears, the alert waits on a human `UPDATE`", and that the finding was "Recorded as an `events.decision_log` `ops-note` (2026-08-26), owned by W5 / the owner." **All three statements are now false.** W5 adjudicated that referral (`8555992d`) on 2026-08-30 and FIXED it rather than re-deferring it: `bigquery/204_probe_funding_stalled_alert_policy.sql` landed and applied live with its `ASSERT` passing, and `ops.alert_policy` now carries the category — 1 row, `latching=FALSE`, against **36** registered categories, not 34. W5 could take what SL3 correctly declined because the change is purely ADDITIVE and `NOT EXISTS`-guarded: the category has never once been raised (0 rows in `ops.alerts`, 0 in the source view, 0 strategies have ever reached PROBE), so there was no live alert whose behaviour it could change — the same pre-registration-before-first-firing discipline SL3 itself applied to the `SHADOW->PAPER` marker and the PAPER stuck-flag widening. **Timing, stated so this is not read as a lapse:** that policy row's `updated_ts` is 2026-08-31 05:37 UTC = 2026-08-30 23:37 MT, roughly three hours AFTER SL3's own 2026-08-30 completion at 20:25 MT, so the 2026-08-31 fire is the first SL3 run that could have observed it.
     - **THE DUTY, which is the part that matters: `ops.alert_policy`'s registered `resolve_rule` names SL3 ITSELF as the owner, and nothing else will ever clear this alert.** That rule is explicit that `latching=FALSE` "only SANCTIONS the resolve" and does **not** make the row self-clearing, and that the category is covered by **no** `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts` rule (those are hardcoded to `missing_dependency` / `missed_run` / `routine_stalled` / `catchup_refire_blocked` / `staleness` plus the roster-notice rule). So the obligation is SL3's, on every fire, and it is this: **for any `strategy_code` carrying an OPEN `probe_funding_stalled` alert that NO LONGER appears in `state.strategy_probe_funding_stalled`** — the funding gap closed, the owner deposit landed, or the probe was withdrawn — resolve it, `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='<strategy_code>; <what closed the gap>; SL3 <run_date>' WHERE alert_id='<id>' AND NOT resolved`. **SCOPE BY `alert_id`**, against the one `strategy_code` just re-verified — never a blanket clear of the category, since two strategies can stall independently — and **NEVER resolve on age**: an aged-out row is indistinguishable from a genuinely-funded one, and the whole condition is a newcomer sitting below its stake floor waiting for capital that may simply never have arrived, which is the aging-alert trap in the place it would cost most.
     - **WITHOUT THIS PIN A FUTURE SL3 WOULD DECLINE THE DUTY ON A CORRECT READING OF THE SHARED RULES — which is why it is stated here and not left to the policy table to carry alone.** The shared Observability section's INCIDENT INHERITANCE bullet grants a routine the verified-clear resolve for **"These two BigQuery-infra categories ONLY"** (`bigquery_quota_exhausted` and a BigQuery-referencing `connector`) and says every other class "stays human-only per the fail-closed allowlist". Read on its own — and it is the text a routine actually re-reads at alert time — that sentence FORBIDS the `UPDATE` above. The authorization is narrower and newer than that sentence: it is the **per-category `resolve_rule` in `ops.alert_policy`**, which is exactly what `bigquery/34_alert_lifecycle.sql`'s fail-closed allowlist exists to carry, registered for this category by W5 on 2026-08-30 and naming SL3. **Where a category carries its own registered rule, that rule governs; the two-category sentence is the DEFAULT for categories that carry none.** Absent this pin the alert would latch in practice despite `latching=FALSE` — precisely the outcome the registration was made to prevent, and invisible, since a stalled PROBE raises no second signal.
     - The message-stability fix above is independent of all this and stands on its own — and the registration's own note records why it is load-bearing here: because `sp_raise_alert_once` dedups on exact `(category, message)` text, an unstable message would have raised a fresh row every day a stall persisted and, before registration, **every one of them would have latched permanently**.
     - **AND THE MESSAGE LITERAL ITSELF DID NOT COMPILE — `''` IS NOT AN ESCAPE IN GOOGLESQL, AND THIS DOCUMENT'S OWN SHARED CONVENTIONS ALREADY SAID SO (SL3 2026-09-01 diligence sweep; reproduced against BigQuery, not inferred).** BOTH spellings of this line's `sp_raise_alert_once` message — the original template above and the STABLE replacement pinned 2026-08-26 — wrote the possessive as `bigquery/62''s`. That is the ANSI/Postgres/Oracle idiom for an escaped apostrophe and it is **invalid in GoogleSQL**, which reads `'…62''s…'` as two adjacent string literals and rejects it: `Syntax error: concatenated string literals must be separated by whitespace or comments`. Reproduced this run against the exact literal, and the corrected text then re-run as a complete `CALL … sp_raise_alert_once(…, TO_JSON_STRING(<row>))` dry-run to confirm it parses end-to-end. **Both spellings are corrected to `bigquery/62\'s`** (a `"…"` or `r'''…'''` literal would serve equally, and is the better choice if this message ever gains a second apostrophe). Three things make it more than a typo. **(i) It is the SAME failure mode as the `TO_JSON(...)` trap pinned in the sentence immediately above** — the `CALL` does not compile on the FIRST stall, which is the only occasion this line ever executes — so the 2026-08-26 revision, whose entire subject was the compile-safety of this one call, hardened the payload argument while re-typing the identical class of defect into the message argument it was replacing. **A pin can carry a defect into the very text that closes one**, and the audit that produced it will not catch that, because it was looking at the argument it had already decided was the problem. **(ii) The rule was already written down and this block broke it anyway.** The shared file-write conventions in this document state **"NEVER double a `'` into `''`. GoogleSQL does not use SQL-92 quote doubling"**, and record that BOTH its failure modes — this syntax error, and a *silent* stored doubled-apostrophe inside a triple-quoted literal — actually occurred on 2026-08-04. So the hazard was known, named, and dated in the same file; what failed is the assumption that a stated convention reaches a literal typed 3,600 lines away. **(iii) Nothing live changed** — the category has never been raised (0 rows in `ops.alerts`, 0 in `state.strategy_probe_funding_stalled`, 0 strategies have ever reached PROBE) — so this is closed before its first firing, the same position as the `SHADOW->PAPER` marker, the `->REJECTED` marker and the `regime_cell` pins. **THE FLEET-WIDE HALF IS NOT CLOSED FROM AN SL3 FIRE, and is explicitly not SL3's text to edit:** when this was written the identical defect stood in FOUR other routines' alert literals — **D3** (two lines, three occurrences), **OPS1**, **Q4** and **A3**, eight executable occurrences across five lines — and three of those (D3, Q4, A3) additionally carried a **bare, undoubled** `'` inside the same single-quoted message (`old_value is the field's value`, `D3's next daily run`, `Q4's quarterly backstop`), which terminates the literal earlier still and is the louder half of the same defect. All eight sites and the bare-apostrophe sites were enumerated and classified that run against the legitimate `COALESCE(x, '')` empty-string uses and the `r'''…'''` triple-quote delimiters, so the finding was a measured list and not a grep count. **RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 (SL3), AND IT HAS MOVED — D3 REPAIRED ITS OWN SITES: five executable occurrences remained at that date, across three lines in THREE routine blocks — `OPS1` (one), `Q4` (two), `A3` (two) — of which `Q4` and `A3` still also carried the bare undoubled apostrophe.** D3 fixed both of its lines on 2026-09-02 and left a `do NOT revert` pin in its own block; its three occurrences are gone. **CLOSED 2026-09-06/07 — W5 REPAIRED THE REMAINING THREE SITES AND DRAINED THE ROW; RE-MEASURED TO ZERO 2026-09-07 (SL3).** W5's SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE on its 2026-09-06 fire corrected every remaining site and resolved the `info` row (`93058867`) at 23:32 MT, its `resolved_note` recording that "Both the doubled-quote AND the bare-apostrophe class were fixed at each site", verified by a 144-call-site re-sweep and by dry-run compiling all three corrected literals against BigQuery. **Independently re-measured this run by CLASSIFYING every `''` line in the file rather than counting matches — the same method this block has used throughout: 20 lines carry `''`, and every one of them is an `r'''…'''` delimiter, a `COALESCE(x, '')`-class empty string, or prose about this defect. ZERO executable occurrences fleet-wide, and zero bare undoubled apostrophes at the three sites.** `OPS1`'s message was closed by the shared rules' *preferred* route — reworded so it needs no apostrophe at all — while `Q4` (four occurrences) and `A3` (five) now carry `\'` at every one, each under its own `do NOT revert` ALERT-LITERAL QUOTING pin; the `task_plan/` slices are byte-identical to the monolith at all three sites plus this one. **The per-site counts W5 repaired are LARGER than the two-and-two this block recorded, and that is a reconciliation rather than a correction of either side:** this block counted the doubled-quote class only, W5 counted that class together with the bare undoubled apostrophes inside the same literals, and each count was right about its own predicate. The pre-repair state is no longer measurable from the tree, so it is recorded as a reconciliation and not re-derived. **This count is stated over EXECUTABLE occurrences only — a `''` inside a literal a routine is instructed to run — deliberately excluding the prose occurrences in which this document discusses the defect, including the ones in this very sentence and their byte-identical copies in `task_plan/`.** That is what makes it a stable measurement rather than the self-perturbing kind SL5's STEP 0 generated-duplicate rule warns about: prose about the defect can be added without end and cannot move this number. The `ops.alerts` `info` row stayed correctly OPEN through the partial D3 repair — a repair by one of the named owners is not a drain while the majority of the sites it names are outstanding — and was then drained in full by the owner venue it was addressed to, which is the OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule working end to end: SL3 measured and recorded, W5 owned and fixed. Recorded as an `ops.alerts` `info` row (`alert_message_literal_uncompilable`) naming every site and the owning routine block, per the 2026-08-28 OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS rule; rewriting four other routines' executable alert text from an incubation-monitor fire is exactly the scope violation this block declines everywhere else.

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — SHADOW/PAPER members monitored, transitions fired (SHADOW→PAPER; PAPER→PROBE enqueued), culls. If nothing: "SL3 evaluated, no incubation transition."

## SL4. Discretionary Retirement Proposer — regular routine

Runs monthly (first trading day), after M4. The REMOVE-ONLY discretionary-retirement scanner, with a hard default-KEEP bias. It adds the missing discretionary-retirement path WITHOUT touching any mechanical kill trigger (drawdown / 30-trade gate / foundation-change / m2m stay exactly as-is in D1/D2/M4). It can only move in the fail-safe direction — retire an edge-decayed / redundant / dominated strategy — and can NEVER spare or continue a strategy a mechanical trigger flagged, so it does not reintroduce the context-aware KILL/SPARE judgment AI_Trading_Foundation.md:384 reserves.

```
Read access scope: Monthly cadence. Read `perf.strategy_daily`, `perf.kill_flags`, `analytics.strategy_vs_park`, `state.strategy_roster` (ADOPTED members), `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy`, `state.strategy_probe_progress`, `state.arsenal_regime_coverage`, `state.arsenal_rails`, `AI_Trading_Foundation.md`, `ops.arsenal_control`, `events.decision_log` (`entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal'` rows), `ops.alerts` (open `category='interim_underperf_warning'` rows). Stages no orders; edits no repo/roster.

Observability: connector pre-flight, `ops.sp_auto_resolve_alerts()`, run-logging, failure alerts — per the shared Observability section. Monitored via run-logging + `cadence_watch`/`period_watch`/`stalled_runs`.

**ARSENAL KILL-SWITCH GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_arsenal_enabled('SL4')` before the dependency gate.** RAISEs + `critical` alert (abort) if the arsenal loop is disabled/frozen.

**DEPENDENCY GATE — SEPARATE and FATAL, do NOT wrap — `CALL ops.sp_assert_deps('SL4', ['M4'], <today>)` BEFORE the start-log.** Aborts (RAISE) + `missing_dependency` critical if M4 has no `completed` run anywhere in the current monthly period — M4 is `monthly_ftd`, so since `bigquery/114_period_aware_dependency_gate.sql` (2026-07-29) the gate is satisfied by any M4 completion with `run_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(in_run_date, MONTH) AND in_run_date`, not only a completion on this exact calendar day. Self-bootstrapping.

STEP 1 — READ RETIREMENT CANDIDACY (objective; default-KEEP). For every ADOPTED strategy read `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy`, which fires ONLY on an objective sustained signal:
   - **edge-decay** — a foundation-citation-status change short of a mechanical foundation-change terminate, AND trailing-12-month deployed-TWR excess-vs-SGOV below a floor, sustained `>=2` quarters;
   - **redundancy** — rolling return-correlation with a peer above threshold where the peer strictly dominates on excess. ENCODED (2026-07-18 audit — `analytics.strategy_return_correlation` (`bigquery/83_correlation_controls.sql`) was built as this signal's substrate but never wired to a consumer; this is its sole read): `SELECT strategy_a, strategy_b, corr, overlap_days FROM analytics.strategy_return_correlation WHERE corr >= 0.7 AND overlap_days >= 40`. For each returned pair where BOTH codes are currently ADOPTED, the signal fires against the DOMINATED member only — the one whose latest `perf.kill_flags.excess_vs_sgov` is STRICTLY lower than its peer's; if either side's excess is NULL/unreadable or they are equal, fire nothing (default-KEEP on ambiguity). A fired redundancy signal counts toward STEP 2 eligibility exactly as `edge_decay_signal` does, PROVIDED `floor_ok AND arsenal_ok AND cooldown_clear` all read TRUE in `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy` (the rails stay binding), and the STEP 3 floor guard applies unchanged — cite the pair + corr + both excess values in `trigger_context`;
   - **dominated-by-newcomer** — a newer ADOPTED strategy covers the same regime cells with strictly better excess.
   No fired signal → no proposal (the default). QUALITATIVE-EVIDENCE INTAKE (consumption-closure audit 2026-07-16 — closes the Q1/Q3/A3 dead channel): additionally query `events.decision_log` for `entry_type='strategy-retirement-signal'` rows from the trailing 2 quarters and `ops.alerts` for open `category='interim_underperf_warning'` rows (D1's 90-day/−15% early signal). For an ADOPTED strategy with such signals from `>=2` rows carrying DISTINCT `source_session` values, or ONE signal PLUS an open interim_underperf_warning alert, treat candidacy as fired for STEP 2 EVEN IF `edge_decay_signal=FALSE`, PROVIDED `floor_ok AND arsenal_ok AND cooldown_clear` all read TRUE in `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy` (the rails stay binding; only the perf-threshold component is supplemented — the proposal still faces the default-KEEP adversarial review). **DISTINCT `source_session` is a mechanical, queryable bar, not "different quarters" (owner directive 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW hardening — closes a gap an adversarial review found: two rows dated into two different quarters by ONE Q1/Q3 catch-up session backfilling a multi-quarter window would otherwise satisfy an "or different quarters" reading of this test even though they reflect one session's judgment, not two independent corroborating cycles).** This is why Q1/Q3's WRITE-ONCE convention (their PART 2 sections above) requires `source_session` on every `strategy-retirement-signal` write to be the writing run's own `<session_id>` (the same literal value that run's Run-logging `sp_log_run`/`sp_routine_end` calls use) rather than a per-write "`Q1 <date>`"/"`Q3 <date>`"-style free-text label: every row a single catch-up session writes, however many quarters it covers, then shares exactly one `source_session` and counts as ONE source cycle here — only a genuinely separate future run (its own session) earns a second. Cite the decision_log `entry_id`s + alert `alert_id` in STEP 2's `trigger_context`. A single uncorroborated signal is only noted in the STEP 4 heartbeat.

STEP 1b — PROBE PROGRESS WATCH (loop-completeness audit 2026-07-16). Read `state.strategy_probe_progress` (`bigquery/73_probe_progress_watch.sql`). For any row with `stuck = TRUE` (>=400 days in PROBE, fully funded, ZERO closed trades and ZERO open positions, no RETIREMENT_PROPOSED within 90 days — a dead signal path, not a slow archetype): treat it exactly like a fired candidacy in STEP 2 — enqueue an `events.queue_events` `PENDING_REVIEW` `review_type='strategy-retirement'` (`conservative_default='KEEP'`, trigger_context = strategy_code + ' probe_stuck: 400+ days funded with zero trades and zero open positions'), write the RETIREMENT_PROPOSED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row + the `ops.roster_change_log` proposal row (this row is also what arms the view's 90-day re-proposal cooldown), and respect the STEP 3 floor guard. An affirmative AR_orc RETIRE verdict routes through the existing D2 step-5 termination handler (closes out and redistributes the idle $2,000 probe stake); a KEEP verdict stamps the per-strategy `cooldown_until` exactly as STEP 2 does. Never a chat question.

STEP 2 — PROPOSE (affirmative-RETIRE-required). For each fired candidacy, enqueue an `events.queue_events` `PENDING_REVIEW` `review_type='strategy-retirement'` (`conservative_default='KEEP'`, trigger_context = strategy_code + the fired signal) and write a RETIREMENT_PROPOSED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row AND an `ops.roster_change_log` row (`change_key='<code>:ADOPTED->RETIREMENT_PROPOSED:<YYYY-MM>'`, `strategy_code=<code>`, `from_state='ADOPTED'`, `to_state='RETIREMENT_PROPOSED'`) — this row is what `state.strategy_retirement_candidacy.cooldown_clear` (**live def `bigquery/81_arsenal_fixes.sql`** — corrected 2026-09-06, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing SL4's `stale_live_sql_pointer`; this pointer read "bigquery/39" until then, but `bigquery/39_beta_adjusted_alpha.sql`:139 carries its own SUPERSEDED-LIVE marker naming 81 as current, and SL4's 2026-09-01 run built a `refs` entry for a nonexistent `bigquery/39_retirement_candidacy.sql` straight off the stale text) reads; without it the 90-day post-KEEP re-proposal cooldown is unenforced. Only an affirmative AR_orc RETIRE verdict routes the strategy to the existing D2 step-5 termination handler; a KEEP verdict writes the ADOPTED lifecycle row + its roster_change_log marker (see AR_orc step 4); the proposal-time roster_change_log row above is what enforces the 90-day re-proposal cooldown.

STEP 3 — FLOOR GUARD. NEVER propose a retirement that would drop the active roster below `state.arsenal_rails.n_min` (=2) — skip, and if the floor binds leave SL1 to backfill a successor candidate.

STEP 4 — HEARTBEAT. Write the monthly `arsenal-heartbeat` `events.decision_log` entry (strategies evaluated, candidacies fired, proposals enqueued) + on any proposal `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('warning','SL4','retirement_proposed', '<code> (<name>) proposed for RETIREMENT — <fired signal: edge decay / redundancy / dominated-by-newcomer / probe-stuck>. AR_orc adjudicates (conservative default KEEP); no action needed from you.', '<JSON per the preamble ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract, with kill_trigger = the fired signal>')`. **`warning`, not `info`** (ROSTER-CHANGE NOTICE contract, preamble) — a pending drop is a roster-membership change the operator learns of by email, not by query. One notice per proposal, at proposal time; the eventual RETIRE or KEEP verdict surfaces separately (SL5 deregister, or AR_orc's decision-log entry).

CHAT OUTPUT: one line — ADOPTED strategies evaluated, retirement proposals enqueued (with the fired signal), floor-guard skips. If nothing: "SL4 evaluated, no retirement proposed."
```

## SL5. Strategy Register & Roster Sync — regular routine

Queue-driven (fires Sun-Thu; no-ops unless a roster-mutation task is due). The D2a-pattern self-executing transition + fanout engine and the ONLY writer of roster MEMBERSHIP — a dedicated idempotent registrar. Never asks a chat question, ever — it self-executes the repo edit / commit / push / live-view re-apply exactly as D2a's autonomous cutover does.

It goes first, unconditionally.

Recorded because this section's own STEP 0 line-pin lesson applies to counts as well as to line numbers — a stale self-measurement stated in the present tense is worse than none, since the next reader cannot tell a drifted claim from a broken invariant. **The class was therefore an instance of ITSELF**: a handoff between two sessions with no shared memory (the raising session and the next cycle's healing session) that leaves REQUIRED values to invention — precisely the condition `bigquery/180` defines — and it fails the same silent way, because a payload missing a key produces no error, just a heal that can never evaluate. **EVERY DATE STAMP IN THIS SECTION IS THE FIRE'S `ops.run_log.run_date` — THE `America/Denver` OPERATING DATE, NEVER THE COMMIT'S UTC DATE (PINNED 2026-09-07, SL5 diligence sweep, MEASURED not reasoned; eight stamps re-dated in the same edit).** SL5's trigger is `25 1 * * 1,2,3,4,5` (`ops/cadence.yaml`) — 01:25 UTC, i.e. 19:25 MT — so **every** SL5 commit is dated one UTC day AHEAD of the `run_date` its own `sp_routine_start` logged. Measured 2026-09-07: the 2026-09-06 fire (`run_date` 2026-09-06, `log_ts` 2026-09-07 01:39 UTC, commit `ced16d7` — whose own title correctly reads "SL5 2026-09-06") stamped **eight** in-section corrections `2026-09-07`, its commit date, while the two sweeps immediately before it (`run_date` 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-03, both verified against `ops.run_log`) used their `run_date`. The cost is this section's own recurring one-hop-off defect applied to PROVENANCE rather than to a citation: the fire that pinned this clause carries `run_date` 2026-09-07, so those eight warrants named THAT run rather than the one that made them, and a session resolving "which fire measured 36 fixtures" against `ops.run_log` lands on the wrong note entirely. **That sentence originally read "today's fire carries `run_date` 2026-09-07" and had decayed within one cycle (CORRECTED 2026-09-08, SL5 diligence sweep).** It was exact on the day it was written and false the next morning, because "today's fire" is resolved by the READER's clock, not the writer's — so the 2026-09-08 sweep read a clause asserting its own `run_date` was 2026-09-07. That resolution is not academic — the `SE-02` lesson below turns on a fixture having landed "~2h AFTER that sweep's own commit", which is unanswerable once the stamp points at the wrong fire. State the rule, then MEASURE compliance separately"), and the section has now committed it on TWO different rules one cycle apart — which is what promotes it from an anecdote about line pins to this section's characteristic defect. Measured 2026-09-09 over this section (`sed -n '/^## SL5\./,$p' Claude_Task_Plan.md | grep -oE "Measured today|this run|this sweep|today's fire|as of this writing|as the tree stands today"`): **14** deictic-shaped hits **at `51104ca`, the tree this sweep measured and NOT the tree that carries this sentence** — because this paragraph's own grep pattern and quoted examples are themselves hits, so the number was perturbed by the act of recording it, exactly as STEP 0's generated-duplicate rule and the retired `cl.from_state` self-count above both predict. **The count is therefore a dated sample and the PROPERTY is the pin: ZERO unanchored deictic USES remain in this section.** That is what a later sweep should re-measure, and it is measured by CLASSIFYING every hit, never by matching a total. **LEGACY ROWS RAISED BEFORE THIS CONTRACT — HEAL THEM, DO NOT STRAND THEM (added 2026-08-20).** A row whose payload is missing `pinned_columns`, or missing the refs entirely, is NOT evidence that the contract is still unpinned — it is evidence that the RAISER predates this paragraph. Treat the payload as best-effort and fall back, in order: (a) any key the payload does carry; (b) the refs and column list named in the row's own `message` text, which every raise to date has stated in prose even when the payload did not; (c) the `git log` for the commit the message cites. Then apply the SAME evidence test — read both sides in the repo and confirm they agree — and resolve or leave open on THAT evidence. **Never leave a row open merely because a payload key is absent**, and never resolve it merely because the key is absent either: an unparseable payload is a reason to read the message, not a reason to skip the row. If after all three fallbacks the handoff genuinely cannot be identified, resolve it with `resolved_note='unidentifiable payload and message; superseded by the 2026-08-20 raise contract'` and re-raise a correctly-shaped row for any contract still believed unpinned — an unreadable row that no future cycle can ever evaluate is the accumulation this non-latching class is most vulnerable to, and re-raising costs one email. **Agree** → `UPDATE ops.alerts SET resolved=TRUE, resolved_ts=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), resolved_note='<both refs re-read at <git sha>; every pinned column agrees — <one-line verdict>>' WHERE alert_id='<id>'` — scoped by `alert_id`, one row at a time, the sanctioned evidence-based routine-owned resolve (ITEM 17 precedent; same discipline as D3's `queue_item_stale` and `queue_venue_claim_unwired` HEAL-RESOLUTIONs). **Disagree** → the contract is genuinely still unpinned: leave the row OPEN and pin the missing side in `Claude_Task_Plan.md` this cycle, then resolve on the next fire against the landed commit. **NEVER resolve on age** — this class is silent by construction (both routines log `completed` either way), so an aged-out row is indistinguishable from a fixed one: the aging-alert trap `phantom_run_completion` documents. **NEVER resolve a row for a different handoff** — the evidence is per-handoff, the same discipline `queue_venue_claim_unwired` keeps per `(item_key, finding_class)`. Scoped to `source='SL5'` deliberately: this is the raising routine's own debt, and any FUTURE routine that raises this category owes itself the same step rather than inheriting SL5's. Best-effort — a failure here can never abort the run, and it never gates the roster work below.
